news.Title: Amazon Wants to Put an Autonomous Flying Robot in Your Living Room
news.Content: This article first appeared on GuruFocus . Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) shares gained approximately 1.5% Tuesday after its Ring division unveiled AI-powered security robots capable of patrolling homes and businesses autonomously. The launch expands Amazon's ambitions beyond traditional security cameras into robotics, potentially opening new hardware and subscription revenue opportunities as competition intensifies across the smart-home market. Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with AMZN. Is AMZN fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator. Amazon's Ring business sells video doorbells, security cameras, alarms and connected home-monitoring services. Its products generate hardware sales and recurring subscription revenue, while integrating customers into Amazon's broader technology ecosystem. On November 10, Ring introduced Ring Robotics, featuring two products: the Ring Drone Cam for residential customers and Ring Rover Cam for businesses. The Drone Cam, priced at $249.99, flies preset indoor routes and can automatically investigate disturbances when connected Ring alarms or sensors activate. Its approximately eight-minute flight time limits continuous monitoring, but automated docking and recharging allow repeated patrols. The Rover Cam, starting at $999.99, uses wheels to navigate commercial spaces and includes a siren, warning lights and two-way communication. Both devices use Ring's AI Pilot technology, combining cameras, sensors and cloud processing to navigate obstacles. Ring founder Jamie Siminoff described the initiative as the beginning of a future where proactive, autonomous protection is something every home and every business can have. The company already benefits from substantial market penetration. According to SmartHome.org, approximately 61% of U.S. households have security cameras, while Ring accounts for 43% of primary security systems identified by surveyed users. However, Amazon has not disclosed expected sales volumes or revenue contributions from the products. Investors Takeaway The Rover Cam begins shipping December 16, followed by the Drone Cam on January 27, subject to regulatory clearance. Investors should monitor initial sales, customer reviews, subscription adoption and whether robotics encourages existing Ring customers to purchase additional products. Privacy concerns, device reliability and regulatory requirements could complicate broader adoption. Competition from Alphabet's Google Nest and other security providers also remains significant. For Amazon shareholders, the opportunity is less about immediate earnings growth and more about building another recurring-revenue business. Strong customer adoption could strengthen Ring's ecosystem, while disappointing demand would limit the financial significance of its robotics expansion. news.Title: 〈陸股盤後〉午後漲幅擴大 三大指數走高
news.Content:
中國股市A股三大指數周三（11日）集體開低，早盤指數分化，滬指表現較弱，創指震盪走高漲幅擴大。AI硬體側午後繼續擴大漲幅，帶動創指很快漲超過3%。

上證綜指周三收盤漲0.46%，報3,680.64點；深證成指漲1.32%，報11,389.74點；創業板指漲3.11%，報2572.07點。

Wind統計顯示，兩市及北交所共3,537家上漲，1,824家下跌，平盤有215家。

兩市成交額為人民幣1.6763兆元，較前一交易日增加1,714億元。

申萬宏源研究所A股投資策略首席分析師傅靜濤在研報中提到，長期，A股處於「兩階段上漲之間2018年級別調整階段」；中期，防禦絕對主導的單邊調整已處於後段，隨後可能是底部主題活躍的震盪階段，這是建構「第二階段上漲」必經過程；短期，超跌反彈動力累積，資金供需平衡重建，歲末年初2027年春季行情可期，超跌反彈更早演繹也在情理中。

傅靜濤說，2027年3～4月前，可能是超跌反彈演繹，A股總體不再創新低窗口；2027年3～4月後，本輪市場調整可能來到底部區域，隨後結構性機會增加、主題活躍，新共識可能在此過程中凝聚。

2027年下半年期待「第二階段上漲」建立。2027年可能出現從資產配置環境、產業趨勢和資金供需共振逆風，轉向共振順風涇渭分明的大拐點。2027年下半年投資機會可能好於上半年，2027年投資回報可能高於2026年。

華泰證券認為後續關注：

一是增量政策落地成效，關注人民幣5,500億地方債結存限額和8,000億政策性金融工具支持項目落實成效。

二是穩市場政策傳導，國常會提出完善資本市場穩市機制，高度關注後續金融管理部門如何部署。

三是外部約束，聚焦美國期中選舉之後內政外交新變化以及中東局勢演變。

四是今年12月中共中央經濟工作會議將為明年政經大年定調，高度關注Q4高層調研和財政貨幣政策信號。

news.Title: 《台股盤後》飆漲1545點，重返44K及十日線
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-11 16:02:51 新聞中心 發佈

美股盤後CoreWeave季報優預期並化解市場對AI基建疑慮、Nasdaq盤後電子盤亦強勢上攻下，台股今(11)日由10月營收創佳績的台積電全場穩盤，加上日經225指數及韓國KOSPI指數亦穩步走高，激勵聯發科、台達電等盤初一度轉弱權值股明顯轉強，且金控股亦適時發揮助攻火力，搭配19大類股中僅觀光餐旅收跌，加權指數終場收在今日最高點44257.15點，飆漲1545.23點或3.62%，重新站上10日線並創下史上第6大收盤漲點，成交量則萎縮至8491.65億元。

美國10月消費者物價指數(CPI)比預期火熱，引發市場憂心聯準會(Fed)恐於12月升息並更積極收緊銀根，同時輝達股價連續第2個交易日下殺，導致美國四大指數10日全面收低。亞洲股市方面，因美股盤後Nasdaq電子盤走強，激勵日經225指數半導體相關股大漲、終場收漲1.31%；韓國KOSPI指數亦同步上漲2.60%。

台股今日台積電挾股利創高與10月營收年增近6成的利多題材，股價呈開高走高，終場以最高價2395元作收、上漲4.81%，收復月線。其餘電子股亦有亮眼表現，創意亮燈漲停，奇鋐、健策分別勁揚逾8%、7%，大立光、欣興、聯發科、聯電連袂走強。

從29大類股表現來看，今日以玻璃陶瓷類股表現最為突出、漲幅達9.10%，塑膠類股漲6.17%、半導體類股也勁揚4.50%，成為推升大盤的三大主力。至於弱勢族群部分，運動休閒、觀光餐旅、數位雲端、居家生活為四個下跌的類股，不過僅運動休閒跌幅逾1%表現最差。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人合計買超202.56億元；其中，自營商買超62.57億元，投信買超147.66億元，外資及陸資賣超7.66億元。

news.Title: 5 AI Heavyweights That Look Too Cheap to Ignore After the Sell-Off
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Alphabet Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

A sharp AI-sector sell-off has left NVIDIA, Taiwan Semiconductor, Micron, Alphabet, and Sandisk trading at historically low valuations relative to their growth prospects.

NVIDIA faces a new, hard-to-measure risk after reports that an alleged Chinese intelligence recruit had contact with CEO Jensen Huang, prompting a board investigation, lawsuit, and FBI scrutiny.

Despite steep discounts and bullish analyst price targets across all five stocks, each company carries distinct risks, including memory-market cyclicality, Taiwan geopolitical exposure, and investor concerns about AI spending.

The AI trade just went through one of its roughest periods yet.

On Thursday, Nov. 5, the Nasdaq-100 dropped 6.36%, its worst day since March 2020, as fears that Democrats' midterm gains could slow the AI data center buildout triggered a wave of selling across chip, memory, and infrastructure stocks.

→ Wall Street May Be Making a Big Mistake With monday.com Stock

Friday's session then brought some relief, even as a stronger-than-expected jobs report pushed the odds of a December Fed rate hike to around 78%. But the calm didn't last long. Over the weekend, a new risk emerged at the center of the AI trade, sending NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) lower again in Monday's pre-market session.

The recent sell-off has left five of AI's biggest beneficiaries—NVIDIA, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM), Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL), and Sandisk (NASDAQ: SNDK)—trading at valuations that look too cheap to ignore. But with uncertainty mounting across the sector, investors must determine whether those discounts represent genuine buying opportunities or signs of deeper trouble.

→ Atlassian Tanks After Huge Run as Guidance Disappoints, But Strength Remains

NVIDIA: Cheaper Than It Has Looked in Years, But With a New Cloud of Uncertainty

NVIDIA closed Friday, Nov. 6, at $186.64, essentially flat for the year and about 23% below its 52-week high.

On valuation, the stock has rarely looked this inexpensive, trading at roughly 24x trailing earnings and under 12x forward estimates, with analysts projecting nearly 70% earnings growth.

→ America's Rare Earth Clock Is Running Out, But the Bottleneck Isn't Where You Think

In its most recent quarter, fiscal Q2 2027, revenue more than doubled to $96.2 billion, data center sales rose 117% to $89 billion, and management guided to about $108 billion for the fiscal third quarter. Analysts have given the stock a consensus Buy rating, with an average price target of $319 that suggests an additional upside of 90%.

Story Continues

But NVIDIA now faces a different kind of risk, one that extends beyond its financial performance and the broader AI sell-off—and one that is hard to measure.

The New York Times and Financial Times have reported that Alice Huang, a former director of Singapore-based NVIDIA customer Megaspeed who reportedly continued to act as a company executive after her resignation, was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to gather information on CEO Jensen Huang. China has denied the claims.

On Sunday, Huang admitted in a memo to employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologized. At the same time, NVIDIA's board launched an independent investigation led by independent directors with outside counsel. The company has previously said Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were ordinary customer contacts, maintaining that customers do not receive sensitive trade secrets or national-security information. In its Nov. 8 statement, the board said it had no reason to believe national security or NVIDIA's secrets had been compromised, although the investigation remains ongoing.

The full extent of the fallout remains uncertain, but the controversy is already attracting legal and government scrutiny.

A shareholder filed a proposed class-action lawsuit on Nov. 9, alleging that NVIDIA and Huang misled investors about the relationship and its potential national-security implications. President Trump also confirmed that the FBI is looking into the matter.

Separately, Megaspeed has faced U.S. scrutiny over allegations that it helped Chinese companies obtain restricted NVIDIA AI chips, raising additional export-control concerns.

Given NVIDIA's size, any lasting damage could ripple across the entire AI trade, including suppliers and partners on this list. Shares fell 4.3% on Monday, Nov. 9, and extended their losses in Tuesday's trading. Fiscal third-quarter results, commentary, and guidance, expected on Nov. 17, now take on added importance.

On the chart, the stock's positioning matches the negative news and sentiment shift over the weekend. The stock now trades below all key Simple Moving Averages (SMA), and below the prior week's low, suggesting that a sustained bottom has yet to be confirmed.

The next area of potential support for the bulls to watch is near $170, where the stock previously found support for almost six months before breaking out to new highs in April of this year.

Taiwan Semiconductor: Pricing Power at a Reasonable Price

Taiwan Semiconductor builds the advanced chips that power the AI buildout, including NVIDIA's.

The company is widely regarded as the most important chipmaker, capturing close to 90% of the advanced semiconductor market.

The stock is up nearly 29% this year, but sits roughly 20% below its 52-week high after the recent sell-off.

At about 17x forward earnings, with projected earnings growth above 31%, its price-to-earnings-to-growth ratio sits at just 0.76. That's an attractive metric and valuation for a company with an impressive record of earnings beats, pricing power, and operational excellence.

As covered by MarketBeat, TSMC has been flexing its pricing power, raising prices on advanced packaging and wafers.

Company insiders have also been buying shares in contrast to the steady insider selling at many tech peers.

TSMC holds a Buy analyst consensus rating with an average target of $533.89, implying about 36% upside.

The company's most often discussed risk is its geographic positioning in Taiwan amid ongoing political uncertainty between China and Taiwan.

From a technical perspective, the picture differs sharply from NVDA's. Following Thursday's sector-wide panic, TSM has sharply bounced off that low. That price action might signal a short-term bottom. Going forward, the bulls will want to see any retests near $360 find support and hold.

Micron: A Deep Discount on Surging AI Memory Demand

Micron Technology has been one of the year's biggest winners, still up more than 145% in 2026.

Yet the sell-off has hit it harder than most, leaving shares just over 40% below their 52-week high.

That drawdown has pushed its valuation to just over 9x trailing earnings, with a forward multiple even lower, at an eye-popping 3.3.

As MarketBeat previously covered, Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue surged 379% on demand for high-bandwidth memory and NAND, and its capacity is booked through 2027.

Memory is a cyclical business, though, and ultra-low multiples often reflect fears that earnings are near a peak. Still, analysts have given the stock a Moderate Buy consensus rating and an average price target of $1,407.88, implying around 100% upside.

Alphabet: A Cloud Leader Priced Like It's Standing Still

Alphabet is down nearly 9% this year and about 30% below its 52-week high, weighed down most recently by concerns over slowing Search growth and surging AI spending.

Yet its cloud business is anything but stagnant, with third-quarter Google Cloud revenue more than doubling to $30.7 billion.

The stock now trades at an attractive trailing price-to-earnings near 15, though that figure is flattered by large investment gains. Its forward multiple of about 19 is a fairer measure, and still modest for a company growing cloud revenue this fast.

Analysts, despite capEx and slowing Search growth fears, remain steadfast, assigning the stock a consensus Buy rating and an average target of $412.51, implying about 44% upside potential.

And on the technical front, the bulls now have a level to work with. $277 held firm for GOOGL last week, having been tested multiple times. Going forward, that's the level and line in the sand that the bulls will want to see get confirmed as the short-term bottom. Break below it, and more downside might follow.

Sandisk: An AI Memory Powerhouse

Sandisk has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI infrastructure boom, but also one of the hardest-hit stocks during the recent sell-off.

Despite remaining up more than 250% in 2026, shares have plunged roughly 65% from their 52-week high.

That dramatic pullback has left the stock trading at nearly 6.5 times trailing earnings and just three times forward earnings—a remarkably low valuation for a company experiencing extraordinary earnings growth.

In its fiscal first-quarter 2027 results, Sandisk reported $11 billion in revenue, up 23% sequentially. Management also delivered strong second-quarter guidance, projecting revenue of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion and earnings of $55 to $57 per share.

Analysts remain overwhelmingly bullish, with an average price target of $2,056, implying nearly 146% upside potential.

One upcoming development worth noting is Sandisk's eight-for-one stock split, scheduled to take effect Nov. 19. While the split won't change the company's underlying value, it will lower the price per share and could make the stock more accessible to retail investors.

Despite those encouraging fundamentals, Sandisk faces the same challenge as Micron: The memory industry is notoriously cyclical, and ultra-low earnings multiples can sometimes signal that the market believes current profitability is unsustainable. If AI-related memory demand slows, supply increases, or pricing power weakens, earnings estimates could come down quickly.

In the short term, though, the stock appears oversold on both technical and fundamental grounds. The first sign of stabilization would be the bulls defending last week's low, with a potential momentum shift and short-term bottom being confirmed if the stock can reclaim and hold above Friday's high, near $912.

Too Cheap to Ignore—or Cheap for a Reason?

Sell-offs like this one rarely distinguish between strong and weak businesses, and that's often where opportunity starts. Each of these five stocks trades at a meaningful discount to its highs, and several have valuations that look exceptionally modest relative to their near-term growth prospects.

But those discounts come with real risks, from NVIDIA's unfolding investigation to memory's cyclicality, Taiwan exposure, and the market's growing impatience with AI spending. The question is whether those risks are already reflected in share prices or whether further declines lie ahead.

The coming weeks could provide important answers. NVIDIA's Nov. 17 earnings report will offer another look at AI infrastructure demand, while developments surrounding its ongoing investigation could influence sentiment across the sector. Investors may also want to watch whether Micron and Sandisk can sustain their earnings momentum, whether TSMC's pricing power holds up, and whether Alphabet's cloud growth continues to justify its rising AI investments.

For now, the opportunity lies in separating stocks that have been unfairly punished from those whose discounts may be justified. Improving fundamentals and stabilizing share prices could help investors identify which of these five AI heavyweights deserve a closer look.

news.Title: Rambus (RMBS) Upgraded to Strong Buy: What Does It Mean for the Stock?
news.Content:
Rambus (RMBS) appears an attractive pick, as it has been recently upgraded to a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy). This rating change essentially reflects an upward trend in earnings estimates -- one of the most powerful forces impacting stock prices.

The sole determinant of the Zacks rating is a company's changing earnings picture. The Zacks Consensus Estimate -- the consensus of EPS estimates from the sell-side analysts covering the stock -- for the current and following years is tracked by the system.

Since a changing earnings picture is a powerful factor influencing near-term stock price movements, the Zacks rating system is very useful for individual investors. They may find it difficult to make decisions based on rating upgrades by Wall Street analysts, as these are mostly driven by subjective factors that are hard to see and measure in real time.

As such, the Zacks rating upgrade for Rambus is essentially a positive comment on its earnings outlook that could have a favorable impact on its stock price.

Most Powerful Force Impacting Stock Prices

The change in a company's future earnings potential, as reflected in earnings estimate revisions, and the near-term price movement of its stock are proven to be strongly correlated. The influence of institutional investors has a partial contribution to this relationship, as these big professionals use earnings and earnings estimates to calculate the fair value of a company's shares. An increase or decrease in earnings estimates in their valuation models simply results in higher or lower fair value for a stock, and institutional investors typically buy or sell it. Their transaction of large amounts of shares then leads to price movement for the stock.

Fundamentally speaking, rising earnings estimates and the consequent rating upgrade for Rambus imply an improvement in the company's underlying business. Investors should show their appreciation for this improving business trend by pushing the stock higher.

Harnessing the Power of Earnings Estimate Revisions

As empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock movements, tracking such revisions for making an investment decision could be truly rewarding. Here is where the tried-and-tested Zacks Rank stock-rating system plays an important role, as it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions.

news.Title: APPS Q2 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Ad Growth, Guidance Up
news.Content:
Digital Turbine APPS reported second-quarter fiscal 2027 adjusted earnings of 18 cents per share, up 20% from 15 cents in the year-ago quarter. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 12.5%.

Net revenues totaled $178.68 million, increasing 27.3% year over year and surpassing the consensus estimate by 7.24%. Strength across the On Device Solutions and App Growth Platform segments, supported by AI-driven advertising improvements, fueled growth. Adjusted EBITDA increased 46% year over year.

APPS' Q2 Revenue Growth Drivers

Digital Turbine's On Device Solutions segment generated $115.6 million in net revenues before intercompany eliminations, up 20% year over year. International revenues grew approximately 50%, supported by higher device volumes and improved revenue per device despite smartphone supply-chain headwinds.

App Growth Platform revenues reached $63.5 million, increasing 42% year over year. This marked the segment's fifth consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and third consecutive quarter of more than 40% growth. DT Exchange revenues increased 42%, while the brand business grew 45%, reflecting stronger advertiser demand and AI-powered optimization.

Digital Turbine, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Digital Turbine, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Digital Turbine, Inc. Quote

Digital Turbine's AI Initiatives Gain Traction

Management highlighted improving advertising performance through its first-party data and AI-powered targeting capabilities. Higher advertiser returns on ad spending supported stronger pricing and fill rates, particularly across premium advertising placements.

The company also benefited from increasing demand for mobile-app advertising and diversification beyond gaming. Nearly 40% of advertiser spending on DT Exchange came from non-gaming partners. Digital Turbine continues expanding its publisher network, particularly across Asia Pacific, while attracting AI-focused applications seeking monetization opportunities.

APPS' Q2 Operating Details

The non-GAAP gross margin contracted 400 basis points (bps) year over year to 43%.

Sales and marketing expenses, as a percentage of revenues, declined to 8.1% from 10.3% in the year-ago quarter. General and administrative expenses decreased to 18.3% of revenues from 24.3%, while product development expenses declined to 5.6% from 7.8%.

Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA increased to $39.8 million from $27.2 million in the prior-year quarter. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded approximately 290 bps to 22.3%, reflecting improved operating leverage and expense discipline.

Digital Turbine reported GAAP operating income of $20.3 million compared with $6.5 million in the year-ago quarter. GAAP net income reached $10.3 million against a net loss of $21.4 million a year earlier.

Story Continues

Digital Turbine's Cash Flow and Balance Sheet

As of Sept. 30, 2026, cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash totaled $51.62 million compared with $43.21 million at the end of the preceding quarter.

Cash flow from operating activities was $18.84 million compared with $14.46 million in the year-ago quarter. Non-GAAP free cash flow increased to $10.46 million from $7.03 million, reflecting improved cash generation despite continued investments in the business.

Total debt, net of issuance costs and discounts, stood at approximately $353.61 million. Management highlighted continued deleveraging, with the net leverage ratio improving to approximately 2.3 times from more than 4 times a year earlier.

APPS Raises Fiscal 2027 Revenue Guidance

For fiscal 2027, Digital Turbine now expects revenues between $670 million and $690 million, up from the previously guided range of $650 million to $670 million. The company reaffirmed its adjusted EBITDA guidance of $145 million to $155 million.

Management attributed the improved revenue outlook to sustained momentum in AI-driven advertising, stronger performance across its platforms and increased partner adoption. The company plans additional investments in data science, machine learning and AI infrastructure during the second half of fiscal 2027 to support future growth.

Digital Turbine's Expanding Global Opportunities

International expansion remains a key priority. Management expects initial revenues from its Orange partnership in the current quarter and anticipates launching services with another Tier 1 European telecommunications operator during fiscal 2027. These partnerships are expected to contribute more meaningfully to growth in fiscal 2028.

Digital Turbine is also expanding its Ignite platform beyond traditional app distribution into AI agents, e-commerce, lock-screen services and other content offerings. Management expects its expanding device footprint and AI-enabled advertising capabilities to support continued revenue growth, while incremental investments could moderate near-term profitability gains.

news.Title: QBTS Stock Down on Q3 Earnings Miss, Revenues Surpass Estimates
news.Content:
D-Wave Quantum Inc. QBTS or "D-Wave", reported a third-quarter 2026 loss of 11 cents per share, narrower than the year-ago loss of 41 cents. The improvement primarily reflected lower non-cash charges related to warrant liability remeasurement. The Zacks Consensus Estimate is pegged at a 10-cent loss per share.

Revenues rose 21% year over year to $4.51 million, driven by stronger professional services and quantum computing as a service (QCaaS) revenue. The figure topped the consensus mark by 14.2%.

Following the announcement, QBTS shares dipped nearly 2% in the pre-market session today.

QBTS Revenue Growth Driven by Services and QCaaS

Professional services revenues increased $1.5 million year over year, while QCaaS revenues grew $0.8 million. These gains were partially offset by a $1.5 million decline in system sales revenues, reflecting a shift in the company's revenue composition.

D-Wave Quantum Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

D-Wave Quantum Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | D-Wave Quantum Inc. Quote

D-Wave recognized revenues from more than 100 customers during the quarter, with commercial enterprises accounting for 48% of the customer base. The diversified customer mix highlights the company's presence across commercial, government and research applications.

D-Wave Bookings and Backlog Signal Future Demand

Third-quarter bookings totaled $1.9 million, declining 19%, or approximately $0.4 million, year over year. Management noted that quarterly bookings can fluctuate significantly depending on the timing of larger customer transactions.

However, bookings for the first nine months of 2026 reached $37.4 million, increasing 611%, or $32.1 million, from the prior-year period. Approximately 59% of the company's remaining performance obligations are expected to convert into revenues within 12 months, while 71% are expected to be recognized within 24 months.

QBTS Gross Margins Contract on Unfavorable Revenue Mix

On a GAAP basis, gross profit declined 11% year over year to $2.4 million in the third quarter of 2026. Gross margin contracted 1,850 basis points (bps) to 52.9%, primarily due to a higher proportion of lower-margin professional services revenues and a $0.2 million increase in non-cash stock-based compensation.

Adjusted gross profit remained essentially flat year over year at $2.9 million. However, adjusted gross margin contracted 1,410 bps to 63.6%, reflecting an unfavorable revenue mix.

GAAP operating expenses increased 84% year over year to $55.9 million, driven primarily by higher personnel costs, stock-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, professional services and marketing expenses.

Story Continues

Adjusted operating expenses rose 72% to $40.5 million. Consequently, adjusted EBITDA loss widened 83% year over year to $37.7 million from $20.6 million, reflecting increased investments in product development and go-to-market initiatives.

QBTS Liquidity Supports Quantum Computing Investments

D-Wave ended September 2026 with $503.4 million in cash and marketable investment securities. The company used $109.0 million in operating activities during the first nine months compared with $53.6 million in the corresponding prior-year period.

During the quarter, D-Wave executed a definitive agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce providing access to up to $100 million in CHIPS and Science Act funding, subject to specified milestones and conditions. The funding is intended to support next-generation annealing and gate-model quantum computing development.

D-Wave Advances Technology and Commercial Partnerships

The company delivered a 4,400-plus-qubit Advantage2 quantum computer to Italy for installation in Como. It also launched a gate-model quantum computing simulator beta program, enabling participants to develop applications using error-aware programming capabilities.

On the commercial front, NTT DOCOMO deployed its second production application powered by D-Wave's hybrid quantum technology, reducing daily peak location registration signals by 65.3% and paging signals by 7.0%.

D-Wave also extended its partnership with SkyWater through a multi-year semiconductor development and manufacturing agreement. A related maintenance-scheduling project demonstrated reductions in lot delays of up to 30%.

Additionally, the company formed a strategic partnership with CGI to support quantum application development across industries and signed a memorandum of understanding with LG CNS to advance enterprise optimization applications in South Korea and beyond.

Our Take

D-Wave delivered mixed third-quarter 2026 results, with a wider-than-expected loss while revenues surpassed expectations. The company's year-over-year revenue growth, supported by stronger professional services and QCaaS revenues, was encouraging. However, contracting gross margins and a widening adjusted EBITDA loss remain concerning. This indicates an unfavorable revenue mix and elevated operating expenses.

On a positive note, robust year-to-date bookings and a substantial increase in remaining performance obligations indicate healthy demand for the company's quantum computing solutions. Moreover, its strong liquidity position and access to potential government funding should support continued investments in product development and commercialization initiatives.

QBTS' Zacks Rank and Key Picks

D-Wave currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

MKS, sporting a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), reported a third-quarter 2026 EPS of $4.18, which beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 14.84%. Revenues of $1.41 billion surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 4.12%. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here.

MKSI has an estimated long-term earnings growth rate of 36.3% compared with the industry's 24% growth. The company surpassed earnings estimates in three of the trailing four quarters and missed on one occasion, the average surprise being 10.12%.

Arista Networks, currently sporting a Zacks Rank #1, reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of $1.2 per share, which topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 11.11%. Revenues of $3.66 million outperformed the consensus mark by 10.41%.

ANET has an estimated long-term earnings growth rate of 22.7% compared with the industry's 21.2% growth. The company's earnings outpaced estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 10.6%.

Docebo, carrying a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), reported third-quarter 2026 earnings of 55 cents per share, which topped the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 3.77%. Revenues of $70.3 million outperformed the consensus mark by 1.10%.

DCBO has an earnings yield of 6% compared with the industry's 3.8% growth. The company's earnings outpaced estimates in each of the trailing four quarters, the average surprise being 25.6%.

news.Title: Lam Research's Gross Margin Hits 52.4%: Can it Climb Further?
news.Content:
Lam Research Corporation LRCX posted a record gross margin in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, driven by stronger demand, a favorable business mix and improved operating performance. The company's non-GAAP gross margin reached 52.4%, up from 52% in the previous quarter. Its GAAP gross margin also improved to 52.3% from 51.7%.

The improvement came alongside strong business growth. Revenues increased 22% sequentially to $8.22 billion, while the non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 40.2% from 38.4%. Management attributed the gross margin improvement partly to favorable customer and product mix, along with continued focus on costs and pricing.

Lam Research's customer support business also provides a useful source of support. The Customer Support Business Group ("CSBG") revenues reached $2.49 billion, rising about 40% year over year. Strong demand for services, spare parts and equipment upgrades can help support profitability as the installed equipment base expands.

The outlook remains encouraging, but further margin gains may be gradual. For the fiscal second quarter, Lam Research expects a non-GAAP gross margin of 52.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point. Management also flagged customer-mix headwinds and near-term supply constraints. Higher investment in research and development, and manufacturing capacity could also limit margin expansion.

Overall, Lam Research has room to improve margins as AI-related chip demand and production complexity drive equipment spending. However, its guidance suggests only modest near-term progress.

Here's How AMAT & KLAC Compare With LRCX on Margins

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Applied Materials' revenues increased 25% year over year to $9.12 billion, while the non-GAAP gross margin improved to 50.4% from 48.9% a year earlier.

Applied Materials achieved its 13th consecutive quarter of year-over-year gross margin expansion, reflecting the increasing value of its materials engineering solutions and continued operating leverage. Its Semiconductor Systems' non-GAAP gross margin improved 190 basis points to 55.4%, showing the profitability of its core equipment operations.

KLA Corporation KLAC competes with Lam Research in process-control and inspection equipment, which helps chipmakers identify defects and improve production yields. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, KLA's revenues surged 28.8% year over year to $4.14 billion, while the non-GAAP gross margin expanded 20 basis points to 62.7%.

Story Continues

For the second quarter, KLA projects a non-GAAP gross margin of 62.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point. Product cost reductions, improved memory efficiency and pricing initiatives are expected to help offset these pressures over time.

news.Title: Why Sandisk Stock Dropped Again on Tuesday
news.Content:
Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock sank 5.4% through 1:05 p.m. ET Tuesday on some discouraging news about the computer memory market -- and this time it has nothing to do with waning artificial intelligence demand, increased data center regulation -- or worries about Jensen Huang's personal life , either.

Instead, this new worry is about Sandisk specifically.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

China rising

More precisely, the worry is about Sandisk losing market share in the NAND flash memory market -- and another company gaining share.

One year ago, according to data from Counterpoint Research, Sandisk was neck-and-neck with Chinese NAND producer Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. Both companies boasted an 11% share in this market, tying them for fifth place behind Samsung, SK Hynix , Kioxia, and Micron . Both Sandisk and Yangtze Memory gained share steadily over the past year, most recently putting them at 13% and 14%, respectively, at the end of Q1 2026.

In Q2, however, CounterPoint reports Sandisk's NAND market share slid back to 11% -- reversing a year's worth of gains. Yangtze Memory, in contrast, held steady at 14%. (Micron gained two points, and SK Hynix one point.)

What this means for Sandisk

Should Sandisk investors panic? I don't think so.

All six of these NAND companies' market shares have fluctuated by one to three percentage points from quarter to quarter over the past year. There's no clear trend of Sandisk losing share, and for the time being at least, I'd reserve judgment on whether such a trend has even begun.

What is clear is that Sandisk stock, trading below 7x trailing earnings and costing less than 4x the profit it's expected to earn next year, remains a very cheap stock. I'd view today's sell-off less as a cue to panic and more as a chance to buy Sandisk stock even cheaper.

news.Title: 5 AI Stock Picks and Performance of Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller
news.Content:
Billionaire Stanley Druckenmiller has been bullish on AI since before ChatGPT launched. He is one of the most closely followed macro investors on Wall Street. He averaged about 30% a year at Duquesne Capital with no losing year, and his 1992 bet against the British pound made more than $1 billion.

Druckenmiller's AI Stock Picks Take a Beating

The AI trade has taken a turn for the worse since the end of the second quarter. Nine of Stanley Druckenmiller's 10 AI stock picks on this list have declined since June 30, with the stocks losing an average of 27.8% on an equal-weight basis through November 9, compared with a gain of about 0.8% for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY). We have included each stock's performance since June 30 in the list below. But did Druckenmiller get out before the crash? We could find out in just a few days, when his family office is expected to disclose its third-quarter holdings. The filing will reveal whether he sold or reduced positions before the latest AI selloff, or held on to stocks that subsequently suffered steep losses.

To find out what Druckenmiller bought and sold, follow Stanley Druckenmiller's page on our website and sign up for email notifications.

Why He Bought Nvidia Before the AI Boom

Druckenmiller told CNBC in May 2024 that his young partner urged him in 2022 to buy Nvidia. He bought it, and a month later ChatGPT launched, so he raised the position substantially. He cut the stake in late March 2024 after a huge run, and he said he is not Warren Buffett and does not hold stocks for 20 years. He called AI a little over-hyped in the short term and under-hyped in the long term.

Speaking of Buffett, we ranked the Berkshire Hathaway holdings with the most room to rise in our list of the 10 best Warren Buffett stocks with upside potential .

Is AI a Bubble? What Druckenmiller Has Said

Druckenmiller has called AI real from the start. In a June 2023 Bloomberg interview, he said AI is real, unlike crypto. He said real secular shifts do not move in 10 months, and that the internet bubble lasted about two and a half years. He wanted to own Nvidia for at least two to three years.

By May 2024, his tone had changed. He told CNBC that AI could be a little over-hyped now and under-hyped in the long term. He compared it to the internet in 1999, when someone who bought the Nasdaq watched it fall 80% before the internet's payoff arrived. He said history could rhyme, and the big payoff from all the AI spending might be four to five years away.

What He Says About AI, Jobs and Inflation

Story Continues

In a Morgan Stanley interview recorded in January, Druckenmiller pointed out that people called every past technology revolution the end of jobs, all the way back to the horse and buggy. He gave radiologists as an example. Machines read prostate cancer pathology as well as or better than humans, but there are more radiologists today than ten years ago, because they now spend their time with patients. He also warned that AI could turn inflationary if governments answer job losses by printing money.

You can click to see the top 10 AI stock picks of Stanley Druckenmiller and their performance. Below we mention his top 5 AI picks as of Q2.

Methodology

Duquesne Family Office's second-quarter 13F showed he is still buying AI stocks. In this list, we rank 5 of those stocks by the value of Druckenmiller's stake at the end of the second quarter, from lowest to highest. For each stock, we track its performance this year through November 9, measured from its January 2 close.

Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ).

You can watch our video to see the full list of 10 AI stock picks of billionainre Druckenmiller by clicking the image below.

#5 Seagate Technology (NASDAQ:STX)

Druckenmiller Stake as of Q2: $117.7 Million

Year to Date Performance (through November 9): +76%

Return since June 30th: -47.5%

Seagate makes the large hard drives that data centers use to store data. Druckenmiller more than doubled his stake in the second quarter by adding 71,300 shares. His fund now owns 122,000 shares, which made up 2.26% of his portfolio, up from 0.59% in the first quarter.

AI creates huge amounts of data, and Seagate's largest drives are in short supply. The shortage lets Seagate raise prices, which has pushed its profit margins and cash flow to records. Its 2027 prices are already locked in, and Morgan Stanley thinks demand could grow even faster than the companies say.

The risk is 2028. Western Digital, Toshiba and parts suppliers are all adding capacity, just as Seagate sets its 2028 prices. Analysts still expect margins to keep rising. If AI spending slows, drive orders would feel it a few quarters later. The stock trades at 11.5 times expected earnings, a low multiple that shows investors expect profits to peak.

Seagate dropped more than 10% in a single day on a report that Toshiba plans to add hard drive supply, because more supply from a rival can weaken Seagate's pricing power. See whether the dip is a buying chance .

#4 Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL)

Druckenmiller Stake as of Q2: $120.2 Million

Year to Date Performance (through November 9): -9%

Return since June 30th: -19.3%

Druckenmiller sold his Alphabet stake in the first quarter and then changed his mind. His fund bought 336,300 shares in the second quarter, and the stake made up 2.31% of his portfolio. Alphabet is one of only two stocks on this list that are down this year.

The bull case is that Google Cloud has become a second growth engine. In the third quarter, Cloud revenue grew 103% from the same quarter a year ago, and CEO Sundar Pichai said demand for its AI infrastructure is huge. Nearly 100 customers use its TPUs, and Alphabet now sells them outside the company. Search revenue still grew 12% from a year earlier. Total revenue rose 25% and operating income rose 30% in the same period. Alphabet also owns about 5% of SpaceX, which went public in June. The stock is more than 30% below its May high, which gives buyers a lower entry point.

Alphabet's free cash flow turned negative in the second quarter for the first time since the company went public, while Search revenue still grew 17% from a year earlier. Find out why investors still like it .

#3 Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN)

Druckenmiller Stake as of Q2: $129.1 Million

Year to Date Performance (through November 9): +18%

Return since June 30th: 12%

Amazon Web Services rents out AI computing power to thousands of companies, and Amazon also builds its own AI chips. Druckenmiller's fund added 495,800 shares in the second quarter and now owns 541,600 shares as of Q2. The stake made up 2.48% of his portfolio, up from 0.28% in the first quarter. His fund also held call options on Amazon shares.

Amazon could benefit even if the AI data center build-out slows after the midterm elections, Wall Street analyst Dan Ives said in a note to clients. He assumes about 10% of the 800 to 1,000 data centers planned in the US do not get built, and he tested a harsher case where 30% are cancelled over the next 18 months, according to the note. In either case, Amazon and other big cloud companies that already have data center capacity running become more valuable, because less new capacity competes with them, Ives wrote. He expects Big Tech spending growth to peak in 2027, earlier than his old forecast of 2028 or 2029, and he expects the big companies to raise about 25% less capital over the next year, Ives said. The AI boom still continues at a slower pace, which he called "hugely bullish" for Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta Platforms.

L1 Capital expects Amazon Web Services spending to push Amazon's free cash flow negative, but the fund says the market is too focused on near-term cash flow. Click to see why the fund stays optimistic .

#2 STMicroelectronics (NYSE:STM)

Druckenmiller Stake as of Q2: $232.4 Million

Year to Date Performance (through November 9): +62%

Return since June 30th: -40.4%

STMicroelectronics is a European company that makes chips for cars and industrial equipment. It now also sells chips to AI data centers, where they manage power and move data. Druckenmiller's fund added 490,000 shares in the second quarter and now owns 3,102,880 shares.

STMicroelectronics bull case moves around a recovery play with an AI boost. Profits fell hard during the car and industrial slump, so the stock offered a chance to buy before earnings caught up. AI data center demand gives it a second growth driver. In its recently reported quarter, revenue rose 17.9% from the same quarter a year ago and beat Wall Street's estimate. Sales in the segment that holds AI and satellite parts grew 46.2% from a year earlier. Management raised its 2026 data center sales outlook and expects 2027 to be much higher. It also expects factory changes to add more than 4 percentage points to gross margin by early 2028.

STMicroelectronics expects its AI data center sales to roughly double next year and is closing four older factories to lift its profit margins, though its power chip business still loses money. Check the risks and the upside here .

#1 Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM)

Druckenmiller Stake as of Q2: $281.6 Million

Year to Date Performance (through November 9): +22%

Return since June 30th: -18.4%

TSMC makes chips for Nvidia, AMD and Apple, so much of the AI boom runs through its factories. Druckenmiller's fund owns 589,680 shares, the largest stake on this list. It made up 5.40% of his portfolio, up from 4.96% in the first quarter. He added 94,400 shares in the second quarter, a 19.1% increase. The stock is up 22% this year through November 9.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) remains well-positioned to benefit from long-term AI growth, regardless of which chip designer emerges as the industry leader. Its technological dominance in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, including its N2 process and CoWoS packaging technology, gives it significant pricing power and a competitive advantage that rivals may struggle to replicate. Demand for advanced chips continues to exceed supply, with production capacity largely booked through 2027. The company also benefits from strong profitability, software-like margins and substantial cash generation. Bulls say the recent semiconductor selloff could present an attractive entry point for long-term investors.

news.Title: What Bitdeer Technologies Group (BTDR) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Bitdeer Technologies Group? Here are five stocks we like better.

Revenue reached a record $320.7 million , up 89% year over year, and adjusted EBITDA rose to $69.6 million. Bitdeer still reported a $125.5 million net loss amid heavy investment.

Management cited about $7.6 billion in expected contracted AI revenue and 332 IT megawatts of secured data-center capacity. AI cloud revenue grew 46% sequentially to $20.4 million, while construction and customer installations at key sites are scheduled to ramp from late 2026 into 2027.

Spending sharply reduced cash to $163.7 million from $456.8 million as quarterly capital expenditures reached $478 million and debt rose to $1.95 billion. Bitdeer is pursuing project and asset-level financing, while lowering its 2026 crypto-mining infrastructure capex outlook to $200 million or less.

4 Blockchain Stocks That Aren't Coinbase

Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ:BTDR) reported record third-quarter revenue as Bitcoin production and co-mining expanded, while management outlined plans to finance a growing pipeline of artificial intelligence infrastructure projects.

Revenue rose 89% year over year to $320.7 million, and adjusted EBITDA increased to $69.6 million from $25.5 million a year earlier. The company posted a net loss of $125.5 million, or $0.46 per share, as it invested heavily in data centers and computing equipment.

→ The Ugly Truth Behind SoundHound's Q3 Results

Beyond the Halving: The Future of Bitcoin Mining Stocks

Chief Strategy Officer Haris Basit said Bitdeer's AI platform represents approximately $7.6 billion in expected contracted revenue: about $4.7 billion from the base term of its Tydal data center lease in Norway and $2.9 billion in AI cloud backlog. The two businesses have different revenue recognition profiles and capital requirements, he said.

AI Cloud Contracts and Tydal Construction

AI cloud revenue increased 46% from the second quarter to $20.4 million. Bitdeer ended September with 4,328 graphics processing units deployed at approximately 95% utilization. The business generated $3.1 million in gross profit, compared with a $2.3 million gross loss in the prior quarter.

→ Lemonade's Revenue Soars 73%—So Why Did Its Stock Turn Sour After Earnings?

Chief Financial Officer Michael Potter said the sequential revenue increase came primarily from pricing and customer mix as utilization of higher-value systems rose. AI cloud annualized recurring revenue was approximately $86 million at quarter-end.

Story Continues

In Malaysia, Bitdeer has sold out the 9.5 megawatts of capacity at its A102 facility under five-year commitments representing more than $800 million in expected revenue. More than 70% of the 21.7 megawatts at A201 is contracted, representing over $1.7 billion in expected five-year revenue. The company expects revenue to begin at A102 in the first quarter of 2027 and at A201 in the second quarter.

→ Anthropic's S-1 Strengthens the Case for Broadcom's AI Growth

Potter said secured AI cloud data center capacity has reached approximately 332 IT megawatts, or about 95% of the company's target for the first quarter of 2028. He cautioned that secured capacity, which includes owned sites and those covered by executed data center services agreements, is not the same as capacity contracted to customers.

At Tydal, phase-one delivery remains scheduled for year-end, with customer installations planned to begin in January. Phase-two data hall deliveries are expected to start at the end of the first quarter of 2027. The lease with Volta covers 121 IT megawatts over 16 years, subject to the tenant's right to terminate without a fee after 10 years.

Potter said Bitdeer has begun the project-financing process. He also said Volta's reported GPU financing removed a major item needed to activate the anticipated letter-of-credit support, with construction completion and operational GPUs among the remaining steps.

Cash Declines as Spending Rises

Bitdeer ended the quarter with $163.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $456.8 million at the end of the second quarter. Capital expenditures totaled $478 million, including approximately $288 million for data center construction and land and about $110 million for SEALMINER production. Total debt rose to $1.95 billion.

Potter said cash declined because the company funded Tydal construction and a land purchase at Rockdale ahead of expected financing. Operating cash flow was approximately $6 million, including customer prepayments. The company also sold $221.5 million of mined Bitcoin, proceeds reported in investing activities.

Management expects customer prepayments and asset-level financing to support AI cloud deployments. Potter said financing for the A102 GPUs was in its final stages, while work was underway on a similar arrangement for A201. Deferred revenue, mostly AI cloud prepayments, reached approximately $342 million at quarter-end.

During the call, Potter gave differing figures for remaining Tydal construction spending, citing approximately $350 million and approximately $250 million in prepared remarks, then about $500 million during questions. He did not reconcile the figures. He said the company would seek at least $500 million in financing and hoped to recover some equity previously invested in the site, subject to market conditions.

Bitdeer raised $58 million through its at-the-market equity program in the third quarter, compared with $457 million in the second. Potter said the company had not recently accessed equity markets but declined to rule out future equity financing.

Mining Growth and Capital Outlook

Bitdeer mined 3,855 Bitcoin during the quarter, up 43% from the second quarter, while co-mining revenue rose 140% sequentially to $59.9 million. Self-mining hash rate reached approximately 82.3 exahash per second at quarter-end.

Power cost per Bitcoin mined was approximately $36,000, down from $49,000 a year earlier, as fleet efficiency improved. Total gross profit was $10.8 million, reversing a second-quarter gross loss, although average power costs rose to 4.7 cents per kilowatt-hour from 4.4 cents.

The company now expects 2026 crypto mining infrastructure capital spending at or below $200 million, the low end of its previous $200 million to $280 million range. The forecast excludes SEALMINER hardware, GPUs, AI cloud and high-performance computing infrastructure. Potter said Bitdeer plans to provide 2027 guidance with its fourth-quarter results.

Founder and CEO Jihan Wu said Bitdeer expects to slow the pace of new crypto-mining capital investment next year while continuing to expand operations. At Rockdale, he said the company plans to seek additional grid power and build new AI data centers on acquired land rather than broadly winding down existing mining operations.

About Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ:BTDR)

Bitdeer Technologies Group is a technology company focused on cryptocurrency mining and related infrastructure. Its business includes operating mining data centers, mining digital assets for its own account, and providing hosting services that allow customers to deploy and operate mining equipment.

The company also develops and sells cryptocurrency mining machines and offers cloud hash rate services, which provide customers access to computing capacity for mining without requiring them to operate the equipment themselves.

news.Title: ‘Baby Berkshire’ Portfolio: 10 Best AI Stocks to Buy According to Warren Buffett Disciple Tom Gayner
news.Content: The recent AI stock selloff has investors asking how long AI stocks will take to win back confidence. Many are looking at old-school billionaires and veteran money managers who have worked through several market cycles. One of the best-known is Tom Gayner, the CEO of Markel Group. Gayner is a staunch Warren Buffett follower, and Forbes titled its 2024 profile of him "Inside a Baby Berkshire Hathaway." This list shows the 10 biggest AI-related holdings in Markel's latest 13F filing. We also ranked the Berkshire holdings with the most upside in our list of the 10 best Warren Buffett stocks with upside potential . How Gayner Became a Buffett Student Gayner graduated from the University of Virginia in 1983 and later took a job at Davenport & Co., a stockbroker in Richmond, Virginia. Soon after, he read about Buffett and became deeply interested in his investing philosophy. In 1990, Gayner left Davenport to join Markel, an insurance-based holding company that the Markel family started in 1930. Markel also owns a large stock portfolio and a group of private businesses. Gayner ran the stock investments, and his first purchase was Berkshire Hathaway stock. He became co-CEO in 2016 and has been the sole CEO since 2023. Why Markel Is Called "Baby Berkshire" Markel uses the Berkshire model. It runs an insurance business, owns a large stock portfolio, and controls a group of private companies. Cash from Markel's profitable insurance business has flowed into Gayner's portfolio every month since 1990, the Wall Street Journal reported in 2015. Berkshire is also the cornerstone of Markel's portfolio. Its Class A and Class B shares made up 6.48% and 5.94% of Markel's reported portfolio at the end of September 2026. Gayner told Barron's that the friendships and network he built around Berkshire's meetings have no equal. See the Berkshire picks with the most upside in our list of the 5 best Warren Buffett stocks with upside potential . Has Gayner Beaten the Market? Jason Zweig, a Wall Street Journal columnist, wrote about Gayner's record in a 2015 column . Zweig also wrote the new commentary for the 2003 edition of Benjamin Graham's The Intelligent Investor , a book Buffett has called the best investing book ever written. Zweig reported that Gayner's stocks returned an average of 11.3% a year over the prior 15 years. The S&P 500 returned 4.2% a year with dividends in the same period. In 2008, Gayner's portfolio fell 34% and the S&P 500 fell 37%. Zweig also reported that Gayner ran the portfolio for less than 0.01% in annual expenses. Story Continues Tom Gayner of Markel Gayner Asset Management Methodology To compile our list of the 10 AI stocks Tom Gayner's Markel Group is holding, we examined Markel's third-quarter 2026 13F portfolio, which disclosed about $12.84 billion in holdings across 145 stocks as of September 30. We selected 10 holdings tied to AI. Alphabet's Class A and Class C shares count as one company. The stocks are ranked in ascending order of Markel's reported stake value as of September 30, 2026, with the largest holding at number one. Why are we interested in the stocks that hedge funds pile into? The reason is simple: our research has shown that we can outperform the market by imitating the top stock picks of the best hedge funds. Insider Monkey's quarterly newsletter strategy selects 14 small-cap and large-cap stocks every quarter and has returned 612% since May 2014, beating its benchmark by 375 percentage points ( see more details here ). #10 Applied Materials, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMAT) Markel Stake as of Q3: $18.6 Million Applied Materials (NASDAQ:AMAT) makes the equipment chipmakers use to build semiconductors, so its sales rise when companies spend more on AI chip factories. Tom Gayner's Markel Group held 36,350 shares at the end of September 2026, which is 0.14% of its reported portfolio. The portfolio data shows no change to the position in the quarter. Cambiar Opportunity Fund said in its second-quarter 2026 investor letter that AI compute expansion and memory shortages extend Applied Materials' growth runway, so see the Cambiar letter here . Applied Materials shares are down about 34% over the past month. The selloff started after the midterm elections, when investors began to worry that a Democratic Congress would make it harder to build new data centers. Fewer data centers would mean fewer new chip factories, and that hurts equipment makers first. Bulls say the fear is too big. Federal lawmakers can write rules, but state and local governments decide whether a data center gets built, and many of them depend on the property taxes and jobs these projects bring. Bulls also say that even a slower build-out still needs a steady flow of new chip factories, and a company that sells one of the widest ranges of chip-making equipment sits at the center of that spending. Applied Materials also holds more cash than debt, which gives it room to get through a slow stretch. #9 Comfort Systems USA, Inc. (NYSE:FIX) Markel Stake as of Q3: $21.5 Million Comfort Systems USA (NYSE:FIX) installs heating, cooling, and electrical systems in commercial buildings, and data centers are a growing part of its work. Markel held 13,000 shares at the end of September 2026, or 0.17% of its reported portfolio. The portfolio data shows no change to the position in the quarter. Parnassus Investments said in its second-quarter 2026 letter for the Parnassus Growth Equity Fund that Comfort Systems is positioned to benefit from accelerated AI investment, so check the Parnassus letter here . Comfort Systems USA (NYSE:FIX) is one of the under-the-radar AI plays in Tom Gayner's portfolio. Data centers run hot, so every new one needs large cooling and power systems that a contractor has to install and maintain. Bulls say that work will keep coming because big tech companies plan to keep spending on data centers, and Comfort Systems also serves hospitals, schools, and factories. Bears point to the stock's drop of about 40% over the past three months, which followed fears that a Democratic Congress will slow new data center projects. A contractor's revenue falls quickly if projects get delayed. #8 Accenture plc (NYSE:ACN) Markel Stake as of Q3: $29.2 Million Accenture (NYSE:ACN) is a consulting and technology services company that helps big businesses build and run AI systems. Markel held 159,400 shares at the end of September 2026, which is 0.23% of its reported portfolio. The portfolio data shows no change to the position in the quarter. Diamond Hill Capital said in its second-quarter 2026 letter for its Large Cap Strategy that Accenture could be an undervalued AI opportunity after its sharp selloff. See the Diamond Hill thesis here . Accenture is an AI play because companies need help putting AI to work, and Accenture gets paid to do it. More than 400 clients started their first advanced AI projects with Accenture in fiscal 2026. Bulls say the stock is still cheap. Investors feared AI would replace consultants, and those fears have faded. The shares trade at about 18 times forward earnings, below their 10-year average of about 26. The lower multiple comes with slower growth. Analysts expect Accenture's earnings per share to grow about 5% in fiscal 2027, in line with company guidance of 3% to 6%, and about 8% in fiscal 2028. Bears say AI can hurt Accenture as well as help it. Baird downgraded the stock after a near 100% gain since June, saying clients could use AI to work more efficiently and give Accenture less work. #7 Cisco Systems, Inc. (NASDAQ:CSCO) Markel Stake as of Q3: $38.3 Million Markel held 355,500 shares of Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) at the end of September 2026, which is 0.30% of its reported portfolio. The portfolio data shows no change to the position in the quarter. The London Company said in its second-quarter 2026 investor letter that strong AI infrastructure orders drive confidence in Cisco. See the full letter here . Morgan Stanley recently downgraded Cisco to equal-weight from overweight, and the reasons apply to the whole AI story. The shares rose 43% over the past 12 months, compared with 14% for the S&P 500. Morgan Stanley says a large part of the AI-driven gain is already in the price. Cisco trades at about 19 times forward earnings, a higher multiple than it has had in the past, so there is little room for the stock to beat what investors already expect. Morgan Stanley also pointed to lower gross margins from Cisco's AI business, and it was worried about the margins on the cloud business. It added that some customers may have bought early to get ahead of Cisco's price increases, which could mean weaker orders later. Morgan Stanley still likes the business itself. It sees several years of double-digit growth, mostly from cloud customers, and says that supports a higher multiple than Cisco has had before. #6 Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) Markel Stake as of Q3: $151.7 Million Markel held 209,163 shares of Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) at the end of September 2026, or 1.18% of its reported portfolio. It trimmed the position by 10.68% in the quarter. Retail investors are debating whether Meta is dead money or the best cheap AI stock. Click to see both sides . Many readers will be surprised to see Meta in Tom Gayner's portfolio. The Wall Street Journal has reported that Gayner looks for profitable companies with good management and a reasonable stock price. Meta is now spending so much on AI data centers that its free cash flow turned negative in its most recent quarter. Bears say Meta's only real moat is its huge base of users, which lets it sell ads at high prices. They say AI models are becoming commodities, because many companies now sell similar ones, so Meta will struggle to earn much from its own. Muse, Meta's new AI model, is growing fast but is still small next to the cost of the data centers behind it. Meta also has no big cloud business to rent out its spare computing capacity, unlike Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet, the Journal reported. That means Meta has to earn back its AI spending through its own apps. Bulls point to those same apps. In the most recent quarter, Meta's average price per ad rose 14% and the number of ads shown rose 10% from the same quarter a year ago. The stock trades at about 21 times forward earnings, close to its own five-year average of about 22. Bulls say that is a fair price for a business that still grows ads this fast. news.Title: Don’t Chase the Arm Stock Dip Yet. What Patient Investors Should Wait for Before They Buy.
news.Content:
Arm Holdings (ARM) just did everything right on paper, and the stock still tanked. The stock fell more than 11% on Thursday right after the earnings report.

In its fiscal second-quarter report, Arm delivered revenue of $1.44 billion, up 27% year over year and above the $1.38 billion analysts were expecting. Adjusted earnings per share hit $0.52, up from $0.39 a year ago and ahead of the $0.47 consensus.

More News from Barchart

Nvidia Stock Could Shed Up to $225 Billion Over Jensen Huang Probe, But Rival AMD's Rally Shows It's Not an AI Demand Problem

Dear D-Wave Quantum Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 10

Dan Ives Sees Just a 15% Chance Nvidia Loses Jensen Huang — But His Removal Could Erase 30% of The Stock's Value

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

So, yes, Arm topped estimates on both revenue and EPS. Still, investors headed for the exit. That's a puzzling reaction, but a closer look at the numbers explains it.

Why Arm Stock is Sinking

The selling momentum was not abated after just one poor session; ARM stock is down by over 42% in the last month, but is still up by nearly 60% for the year.

The stock reached a 52-week high of over $450 earlier this year, fueled by the soaring frenzy surrounding artificial intelligence, but has returned most of it. That indicates that the rally was a weak one.

Add to that a frosty atmosphere behind them. The demand for phones is being impacted by high pricing of memory, which has been under pressure in the broad chip industry. In addition, the royalties failed to take off. The increase in royalty revenue was 8% to $670 million, which was less than the estimated 13% increase Arm told investors in July.

Turning to valuation, Arm isn't cheap, even after the drop. Its Price-to-Earnings (P/E) is 83x, far higher than the sector median of 21x, while its Price-to-Sales is 33x, compared to the sector median of 3.1x. These stretched ratios indicate ARM shares trade at a significant premium, making the stock very costly for new investors.

What's Really Happening Under the Hood

The most important thing is that it was an authentic beat, but it wasn't from the right spot. The numbers for licenses, which pay for the rights to use equipment, increased 50% to $773 million, compared with only an 8% increase for royalties, the category that correlates with the number of chips sold.

Licensing is lumpy. Investors pay the stream of revenues called royalties. Last fiscal year, smartphones accounted for approximately 43% of the royalty revenue, while the actual revenue from royalties was relatively unchanged.

Story Continues

Guidance didn't help either. Third-quarter Arm revenue is expected at $1.54 billion, while adjusted earnings per share (EPS) are forecast at $0.56, still just a hair below the midpoint of the $1.53 billion and $0.55 reported consensus.

Arm's Bigger Plan Beyond Phones

The good news is that Arm is no longer just a licensor. Its first real chip, the Arm AGI CPU, is built for agentic AI, with Meta Platforms (META) as the lead customer and shipments starting in the fiscal fourth quarter.

Arm now expects up to $2 billion in cumulative AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028, double its prior forecast. The long-term target is $15 billion a year by fiscal 2031.

Elsewhere, data center royalties doubled and now make up about a quarter of the total, while physical AI royalties grew 50% on auto strength. However, first-generation gross margins should be just 30% to 40%, and real volume doesn't arrive until fiscal 2028.

Wall Street Can't Agree on Arm Stock

There is a divide among analysts, and it is growing. Among the most vocal bears is Goldman Sachs, which still has a $160 target and a Sell rating. It argues that the price is slow to move and more often than not, that price is determined by licensing, not royalties or by using an AGI CPU.

More conservative groups have been Morgan Stanley, which maintained an Overweight rating on the stock but reduced its target price to $245 from $255. It noted that results were solid, with a 50% increase in licensing revenue to $773 million, as well as several AGI CPU purchase orders and a new SoftBank project.

Lee Simpson of Morgan Stanley held an Equal-Weight rating and a $212 target, noting execution concerns with scaling up production of CPUs. Susquehanna's Mehdi Hosseini maintained a Positive rating on Arm and kept the $320 target unchanged, topping their list with Arm's aim to ramp up to $2 billion of AGI CPU sales by fiscal 2028.

The 32 analysts have a consensus "Moderate Buy," and the 12-month average price target is $270, which suggests the stock could climb up to 74% from here. We have targets from $130 to $480, so no one agrees on what Arm is worth.
