news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: Bloom Energy, Skyworks Solutions and Quanta Services
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 9, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Bloom Energy BE, Skyworks Solutions SWKS, Quanta Services PWR and Micron Technology MU.

AI Stocks Plunge: Buy, Hold or Sell?

It has been a brutal week for some of the hottest stocks in the market, particularly those tied to artificial intelligence, semiconductors and the enormous infrastructure build-out supporting the industry.

On Thursday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged more than 12%, its second-worst day on record, while the Nasdaq fell 5.5% and the S&P 500 dropped 4.4%. The selling was widespread, with some of the market's biggest winners suffering extraordinary one-day losses.

And all of this came just days after the midterm elections delivered a sweeping victory for Democrats, raising concerns about the future of AI infrastructure investment.

Today, technology and semiconductor stocks are bouncing sharply, offering some relief after the dramatic selloff. But investors are left with a difficult question: Is this an opportunity to buy the dip, or the beginning of the end for the AI bull market?

I certainly can't say for sure, but the evidence doesn't suggest the AI boom is over. In fact, I think there are some compelling opportunities emerging, though investors need to be selective.

Below, I will lay out the current setup and share why I think Bloom Energy , Skyworks Solutions and Quanta Services stand out.

What Really Caused the AI Stock Selloff?

The prevailing explanation for this week's selling is fairly straightforward. Democrats swept the midterm elections, the party is viewed as less friendly toward AI infrastructure development, and investors are suddenly concerned that tighter regulations could slow the build-out.

There is certainly some truth to that narrative. Opposition to data centers has been growing, particularly around electricity costs and the strain that new facilities place on local power systems.

However, I think the more important explanation is positioning.

The AI trade had become incredibly crowded, with enormous amounts of capital, much of it leveraged, concentrated in a relatively narrow group of companies.

When those positions begin moving against investors, selling can quickly become self-reinforcing. Losses force funds to reduce exposure, which drives prices lower and creates even more selling.

There is growing evidence that this is exactly what happened. Several hedge funds have suffered severe losses, with reports of managers cutting risk and reducing investment teams.

Story Continues

And importantly, the cracks were appearing well before the election.

Memory stocks began showing signs of weakness over the summer, while the Nasdaq had been gradually slipping since early October. The election may have been the catalyst that accelerated the selling, but I don't think it was the underlying cause.

Is the AI Bull Market Actually Over?

Despite the sharp deterioration in stock prices, I remain constructive on the broader outlook.

The economy continues to show considerable strength, and the bull market has been broadening beyond the handful of technology giants that initially drove the advance.

Meanwhile, the latest earnings season has been overwhelmingly positive. Earnings growth has been spreading across sectors, and corporate fundamentals generally remain healthy.

Most importantly, the AI infrastructure build-out continues to represent an enormous source of economic activity.

The hyperscalers have committed extraordinary sums of capital to data centers, semiconductors, networking equipment and electrical infrastructure. Current spending plans continue to point toward another substantial year of investment in 2027.

Of course, political risks shouldn't be dismissed. New restrictions on data center construction could delay projects and increase costs, particularly in states where opposition has intensified.

But I have a difficult time believing that Washington can simply bring this build-out to a halt. There are powerful economic and strategic incentives behind AI development, and plenty of states will welcome the investment, employment and tax revenue that comes with these projects.

The bigger risk, in my view, would be a meaningful deterioration in the economics of AI itself, followed by cuts to capital spending and earnings expectations.

So far, we haven't seen convincing evidence of that.

AI Stocks: Buy, Sell or Hold?

For investors who have held through this drawdown, I don't see a compelling reason to abandon fundamentally sound positions simply because prices have fallen sharply.

Selling after a violent deleveraging event is often a poor decision, particularly when the underlying earnings outlook remains intact. For investors who were underweight the sector or trimmed exposure during the rally, I think opportunities are beginning to emerge.

However, I am certainly not calling Thursday the bottom. Markets can remain volatile after this kind of liquidation, and some of the hardest-hit stocks may need considerable time to recover.

Micron Technology is a good example. While I remain constructive on the company's longer-term outlook, the stock has broken down from a large consolidation pattern. That is not the kind of technical setup I want to chase.

I would rather wait for Micron to establish a new base before considering an entry.

Instead, I'm looking for stocks with improving earnings estimates and technical setups that are holding up relatively well.

Bloom Energy Stock: A Direct Play on AI Power Demand

Bloom Energy manufactures fuel-cell systems that generate electricity on-site, allowing customers to secure power without relying entirely on the traditional electrical grid.

Its technology is particularly attractive to data centers, utilities and industrial customers that need substantial amounts of reliable electricity, often on accelerated timelines.

Energy has become one of the most important constraints on the AI infrastructure boom.

And I suspect an increasing share of data center electricity demand will need to be met through dedicated generation rather than simply adding more strain to public power systems. Bloom is one of the most direct ways to invest in that shift.

The fundamental outlook is exceptionally strong.

Bloom currently holds a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , with earnings estimates rising dramatically over the last month. Current quarter estimates have increased 39%, while full year estimates are up 23.3% and next-year estimates have risen 13.35%.

Revenue is projected to grow 125% this year and another 63% next year. Earnings growth is even more impressive, with expectations for increases of 338% and 70.9%, respectively.

At roughly 50x forward earnings, the valuation is certainly demanding, but I think the growth outlook goes a long way toward justifying that premium.

More importantly, the technical setup is attractive.

Following the recent selloff, Bloom has pulled back toward a key support level around $160, which has held so far.

That gives investors a relatively clear level to manage risk against. A sustained break below $160 would weaken the setup considerably, but as long as support holds, I think the risk/reward favors buyers.

Quanta Services Stock: The Infrastructure Builder

Quanta Services offers a somewhat different way to participate in the AI infrastructure boom.

The company is one of North America's largest specialty infrastructure contractors, building and maintaining electrical transmission lines, substations, grid connections and other essential power infrastructure.

And its business extends well beyond AI, with exposure to utilities, renewable energy, underground infrastructure and communications.

Whether electricity comes from the public grid or dedicated generation, somebody has to build the infrastructure required to deliver it. Quanta is exceptionally well positioned to benefit from that demand.

The numbers are impressive.

Quanta carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) , with nearly unanimous upward earnings revisions. Current year estimates have increased 6.45%, while next year estimates are up 7.7%, including upgrades within the last week.

Revenue is expected to grow 43.4% this year and 18% next year, while earnings are projected to increase 62.7% and 18.4%, respectively.

Its latest quarterly results reinforced that momentum, with management reporting a record $63.7 billion backlog and raising its full-year outlook.

Shares trade around 29.1x forward earnings, which is not especially cheap, but reasonable considering the growth outlook and visibility into future demand.

Of the three stocks discussed here, Quanta may have the cleanest technical setup.

Shares have pulled back toward the bottom of a declining channel, creating an attractive potential entry point with a clearly defined risk level.

Skyworks Solutions Stock: A Semiconductor Recovery Play

Finally, Skyworks Solutions offers an opportunity that extends beyond the AI infrastructure trade.

Skyworks develops analog, radio-frequency and mixed-signal semiconductors used across smartphones, automotive systems, communications equipment and industrial applications.

The company recently completed its combination with Qorvo, creating a much larger semiconductor business with expanded exposure to defense, automotive, infrastructure and emerging physical AI applications.

I've been highlighting the developing recovery in analog semiconductors for the last couple of months.

Unlike some of the more speculative AI infrastructure names, analog chip companies benefit from a broader improvement in industrial activity and economic growth.

And that diversification is especially appealing in the current environment.

Skyworks also has some interesting AI-specific opportunities. In its November 3 earnings release, management highlighted new timing design wins in AI data center networking and the beginning of shipments of high-performance clocks for hyperscaler systems.

The company reported standalone quarterly revenue of $1.046 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.28 per share.

Meanwhile, earnings estimates have been moving higher, with unanimous upward revisions, including some within the last seven days. Shares currently carry a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) .

The combination of improving semiconductor demand, merger synergies and expanding exposure to AI infrastructure makes Skyworks an attractive way to participate in the next phase of the cycle without relying exclusively on hyperscaler capital spending.

What's Next for AI Stocks?

This week's selloff was extraordinary, but I don't see enough evidence to conclude that the underlying AI investment cycle has fundamentally changed.

However, I do think this correction raises an important question about what the next phase of the AI bull market might look like.

We are already roughly four years into this boom, and much of the early gains have been concentrated in the companies building the infrastructure behind AI. Those businesses should continue to benefit from substantial investment, but that doesn't necessarily mean they will remain the biggest winners in the stock market.

After all, AI is a paradigm-shifting technology that will eventually be integrated throughout virtually every corner of the economy. As adoption spreads, the investment opportunities are likely to evolve as well, potentially shifting toward the companies putting that infrastructure to productive use.

In other words, the stocks that led the market over the last several years may not be the same ones that lead over the next several.

I will be watching closely for signs of that transition, particularly in earnings estimates and the Zacks Rank. If revisions begin deteriorating across the infrastructure leaders while improving elsewhere, that could provide an early indication that market leadership is shifting.

For now, I remain constructive on the broader AI outlook and view this week's selling primarily as a positioning washout. But I also think investors need to remain flexible. The long-term opportunity is enormous, though the best way to participate in it through the stock market may look quite different in the years ahead.

news.Title: 華邦電布局EUV，拚2030年導入
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-09 10:59:42 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電（2344）持續推進高雄廠擴建及製程升級，總經理陳沛銘(圖左)表示，14奈米製程將分為不使用及使用極紫外光（EUV）的兩代技術，若開發順利，預計2030年導入EUV。他也強調，日前通過的700多億元投資，涵蓋Module B土建、機電設施及部分長交期設備，正常交期的投資金會陸續加進來，因此該金額並非整個Module B的總投資金額，後續仍將依製程與設備需求分階段規劃。

陳沛銘指出，華邦電與ASML就EUV的合作已進行約三年半，目前派員赴ASML受訓、試跑及量測，為後續製程導入做準備。設備廠承諾予華邦首台EUV機台約兩年可以給，後續機台依現在交期要約三年半。隨著線路微縮，傳統多重曝光須反覆確保對位精準，EUV有助減少曝光步驟、縮短製程時間並改善良率。至於新廠設備配置，仍須考量16奈米與14奈米製程共用性、金屬層數等因素，現階段先安排交期較長的設備，整體配置仍有調整空間；建廠所需機電、配管及後續二次配工程人力短缺，也是擴產面臨的挑戰。

成熟規格記憶體方面，陳沛銘特別提及，今年公司車用產品的成長亦突出，車用記憶體約占全球記憶體市場3%至4%，隨國際大廠縮減DDR3、DDR4及LPDDR4供應，客戶積極尋求長期供貨，能見度因此特別提高。他特別指出，部分需求來自仍採用這些規格的新平台，並非僅為相容舊平台；過去須主動向客戶推廣，如今則有更多客戶上門洽談供應安排。

展望第四季，陳沛銘表示，記憶體價格仍將上漲，華邦電營收可望續增，但成長幅度將較前幾季縮小。終端市場方面，手機、PC及電視需求仍在修正，部分客戶透過調漲售價維持營業額，實際銷量及產能利用率卻降低，也有客戶調整記憶體配置以因應成本上升。他認為，延後的換機需求仍有回補可能，但後續走勢仍須觀察，不能將目前的漲價行情視為會持續向上。

news.Title: Buy the dip or wait? BofA maps out 3 scenarios for chip stocks and top picks
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Bank of America sees a potential recovery in semiconductor stocks in early 2027 as improving U.S. policy clarity, corporate buybacks and relatively attractive valuations help ease concerns over artificial intelligence spending, although investors may need to wait for earnings estimate cuts before the sector finds a durable bottom.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) has already fallen 37% from its recent peak, compared with an average correction of 32% during previous downturns. The bank said indiscriminate selling driven by fears of slowing AI capital expenditure could begin to run its course by early 2027, with congressional policy developments and share repurchases helping restore confidence.

Semiconductor stocks trade at 13.7 times forward earnings, a 22% discount to the S&P 500's 17.7 times multiple. A return to the historical trough valuation of around 12 times earnings would imply at most another 12% downside, according to BofA. The bank also highlighted buyback support from Lam Research, which has a $25 billion programme, ongoing repurchases by Nvidia and Micron's planned buyback start on December 9.

Previous semiconductor downturns suggest the sector typically declines six to nine months ahead of the fundamental earnings turn, before recovering as earnings estimate reductions become reflected in valuations. The SOX has gained an average of 42% during previous recoveries after those cuts were priced in.

BofA sees the late-June 2026 market peak as a potential signal that earnings estimate reductions could begin in the first quarter of 2027, as companies adjust second-half spending plans. However, the bank cautioned that cheaper valuations alone may not be sufficient to restore confidence, with actual earnings cuts likely needed to establish a sustainable floor.

AI spending remains the biggest swing factor

U.S. cloud capital expenditure is currently running at an annualised rate of about $1.2 trillion, with forecasts pointing to more than $1.5 trillion in 2027. If spending stabilises at current levels rather than accelerating, it would represent a roughly 20% downside against 2027 capital expenditure expectations.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

That scenario could reduce planned AI infrastructure deployment to around 30 gigawatts from more than 40 gigawatts in BofA's baseline assumptions. At an estimated $40 billion per gigawatt of investment, the adjustment could create substantial pressure on semiconductor revenue and earnings.

Story Continues

A 20% reduction in projected capital expenditure could translate into more than 20% lower sales and a 35% to 40% earnings-per-share headwind for AI-focused semiconductor companies. Nevertheless, BofA said spending reductions could disproportionately affect future land, power and data centre construction, while newer and more efficient chips, including Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform, remain investment priorities.

BofA outlines three scenarios and top stock picks

Baseline case: The sector faces around 10% further downside before reaching a trough in the first quarter of 2027. The bank favours leading companies across computing, networking, semiconductor equipment, memory and analog chips. Its picks include Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Credo Technology, Marvell Technology, Astera Labs, Lam Research, KLA, Micron, Texas Instruments, Analog Devices and ON Semiconductor.

Bear case: A downturn extends into mid-2027 as AI capital expenditure weakens more decisively. Defensive companies, including electronic design automation providers Cadence Design Systems and Synopsys, high-free-cash-flow analog chipmakers Texas Instruments and Analog Devices, and less AI-exposed NXP Semiconductors, could outperform.

Bull case: A sharp recovery in AI investment drives stronger gains in higher-beta memory, optical networking, quantum computing and CPU stocks. BofA highlighted Micron, Credo Technology, Marvell Technology, AMD and Arm among potential beneficiaries.

Despite the recent selloff, BofA believes semiconductor valuations already reflect considerable scepticism about the AI investment cycle. The sector trades at a 22% discount to the broader market, compared with a 15% premium during the AI-driven rally. The key question for investors is whether earnings revisions and greater visibility on capital expenditure will provide the catalyst for a recovery, potentially shifting market attention towards a renewed AI spending cycle in 2028.

news.Title: Intel, Arm, and Marvell Have Each Been Cut in Half Since June. Only 1 Is a Stock I'd Buy Now.
news.Content:
Intel (NASDAQ:INTC), Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM), and Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) all set record closes in June. Five months later, each stock is worth less than half as much.

Intel closed at $58.27 on Nov. 4, off around 59% from $140.94, its record close on June 22. Arm ended that day at $191.80, around 56% under its June 18 record close, and Marvell finished at $159.80, about 50% below where it closed on June 4.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

All three fell between around 4% and 7% on Nov. 4 alone, then slid further on Nov. 5. Investors were weighing whether Democrats' midterm wins might slow the build-out of artificial intelligence data centers, especially after Texas elected a governor who campaigned for a moratorium on new ones.

Falls this steep can make all three look like bargains. But each stock is still up over 40% in 2026. And only one of them expects its sales growth to keep speeding up, even as its stock got cheaper.

Marvell is that one, and it's the only one of the three I'd buy right now.

Image source: Getty Images.

Intel's PC problem

Intel's third quarter was strong, with revenue up 21% year over year. The problem is the outlook it gave on Oct. 29. Intel sees non-GAAP (adjusted) earnings of $0.25 per share for the fourth quarter, under half the $0.52 it earned in the third quarter.

PCs are the biggest reason. Higher memory prices have pushed up what new PCs cost, and Intel expects revenue in its PC chip segment to drop over 20% from the third quarter. Its chief financial officer, David Zinsner, sees the weakness lasting until at least mid-2027.

Yes, demand for Intel's server chips still tops what it can supply. But at around $54, Intel stock trades at around 36 times the earnings expected for 2026 and about 30 times the earnings expected for 2027.

Is Arm's royalty slowdown priced in?

Arm reported its fiscal 2027 second quarter (the three months ended Sept. 30) on the evening of Nov. 4. Revenue climbed 27% year over year to $1.44 billion, and its adjusted earnings per share increased 33% to $0.52.

The figure I'd follow most closely, though, is royalty revenue (the fees Arm gets for every Arm-based chip its partners ship). Royalties grew just 8% from a year earlier to $670 million, a sharp slowdown from 22% growth in fiscal Q1. Arm said memory prices hit the smartphone market and offset some of its gains elsewhere.

Story Continues

Licensing revenue, however, jumped 50% to $773 million, and management called licensing an important leading indicator of future royalty growth.

Sure, that might prove true. But at around $170, Arm stock trades at around 56 times its expected earnings for next fiscal year (ending March 2028). Even after a drop of around 60%, investors paying that price are arguably relying on royalties to speed up again soon.

Marvell's sales are speeding up

Marvell's numbers are going the other way. Its revenue growth has climbed each quarter of fiscal 2027 so far, from 28% year over year in the first quarter to 37% in the second (through Aug. 1). On Nov. 2, Marvell said fiscal third-quarter revenue is tracking with its $3.15 billion forecast, now within 2% either way. That'd be around 52% above the year-ago quarter. What's more, Marvell's August forecast called for $1.10 in adjusted earnings per share, up around 45% from $0.76 the year before.

The same day, Marvell agreed to buy optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) in an all-stock deal that values Lumentum at around $115 billion, including its debt. Lumentum shareholders would get 4.5 Marvell shares for every Lumentum share, leaving today's Marvell shareholders holding around two-thirds of the combined company. Closing is expected in the first half of 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approval.

At around $141, Marvell stock trades at around 19 times the earnings expected for fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028), based on Marvell's business alone.

Which one would I buy?

Intel's server chips and Arm's licensing business are each doing well. But Intel's profits are set to fall steeply this quarter, and Arm's royalty growth just slowed to 8%. At today's prices, I think both stocks still cost too much for these problems.

Marvell is the only one of the three whose latest forecast calls for its sales growth to speed up again. And based on next year's expected earnings, its price-to-earnings ratio is around a third of Arm's.

In the end, I think Marvell stock is worth buying here, maybe a bit at a time as the Lumentum deal moves toward closing.

news.Title: The 8x P/E AI Play: Why Silicon Motion (SIMO)’s Deep Discount Makes It a Strong Buy
news.Content:
We just published the list of 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires and Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ:SIMO) ranked 9th on the list.

In the first half of the year, memory was the hottest AI trade. Hyperscalers poured billions of dollars into data centers where high-bandwidth memory was one of the tightest bottlenecks in the supply chain. Most of the memory stocks rallied as a result, though the returns have been muted in the second half of the year so far, accompanied by high volatility.

Some on Wall Street say memory makers are sold out till 2030. Others say only till 2028. While the exact status of the industry can be debated, there's little doubt about the willingness of stock market investors to pay a higher multiple for memory stocks. This debate has been done to death, and memory makers continue to trade at extremely low forward earnings multiples, implying that the earnings cycle has peaked.

So what's the truth? Is it the end of the boom? Or is the structural shift in the memory business finally here? If you would rather avoid the high-risk nature of AI stocks, particularly memory and storage, you could look at companies that are doing the exact opposite, i.e., bringing in healthy cash flows and carrying low debt in our list of 10 Stocks With Low Debt and Strong Free Cash Flow .

But if you want exposure to the best memory stocks, read on. In my quest for the answer to the above questions, I reached out to a person who regularly interviews industry experts to find out answers to questions like these. I asked a famous Substack and X analyst, P Equity Research , whether 'this time was really different'. Here's what he had to say:

"There are essentially 3 important conditions these memory makers set in their LTAs: volume, price, duration. They are all negotiating LTAs to fix volume, a price floor, and duration of contract to get rid of past boom and bust cycles in the industry. As long as the Capex cycle holds strong, yes, they are sold out for 2028 and will be potentially beyond that."

So how are billionaire investors treating memory stocks with so much negativity surrounding the business? That's exactly what I wanted to find out with my article 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires.

Close-up of Silicon Die are being Extracted from Semiconductor Wafer and Attached to Substrate by Pick and Place Machine. Computer Chip Manufacturing at Fab. Semiconductor Packaging Process.

To come up with my article 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires, I first looked up multiple memory ETFs to list all memory stocks. In this list, I include stocks that derive at least 30% of their revenue from memory-related products and services. My list also bundles memory and storage stocks together. That is because some storage types also utilize memory chips and, more importantly, they face the exact same cyclicality that memory stocks are notorious for. They are listed in ascending order of the number of billionaires holding them in their portfolios.

Story Continues

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation (NASDAQ: SIMO ) sits close to the memory makers without actually making memory. Its chips run the flash storage in SSDs and phones, so when memory demand rises or falls, Silicon Motion's sales tend to move in the same direction. High memory prices, which are a big reason that memory stocks have rallied so far this year, have also hurt Silicon Motion. Its phone storage chip sales fell 10% to 15% from the previous quarter, partly because phone makers are struggling to keep their devices affordable with memory this expensive.

Moving Beyond Smartphones

The company's overall performance has been strong, though. Last quarter, revenue jumped 131% to a record $560.2 million, beating the $529.1 million estimate. Earnings of $4.35 per share also came in well ahead of the $3.33 expected. The fastest growth came from storage products for cars and enterprise servers. That business has skyrocketed, growing about 27 times from a year ago and 75% from just the last quarter. During the same quarter last year, it made up 4% of total revenue. Now, that's grown to over 40%. It also recently finished designing a faster storage chip for AI data centers, and plans to send samples to the biggest cloud companies for testing in early 2027. If the tests go well, Silicon Motion could land some big orders. Management expects revenue to grow at least 40% in 2027.

Priced for a Downturn That Hasn't Arrived

Silicon Motion's stock looks cheap for a company growing this fast. At about 13x forward earnings, it trades roughly 32% below its 5-year average, while its price-to-sales ratio sits right in line with its history. Analysts expect earnings to nearly quadruple this year and grow another 58% in 2027. Based on those earnings, the P/E would fall to around 8x next year and close to 6x by 2029. When multiples are so low, it usually means that investors expect profits to shrink once the memory cycle cools. The balance sheet is decent. Silicon Motion carries $1.13 billion in debt against $846 million in cash. If demand from cars and AI keeps growing, I think this discount looks too steep.

Hedge fund interest has dropped, with the number of holders of Silicon Motion falling from 48 in Q1 to 34 in Q2. The value of their stakes also dropped from $901.7 million to $738.3 million.

Silicon Motion's sales still swing with the memory cycle, and its phone business shows how quickly high prices can hit demand. If that sort of volatility makes you uneasy, see our 10 Best Bear Market Stocks to Invest In Right Now for companies built to hold up even when markets turn rough.

While we acknowledge the risk and potential of SIMO as an investment, we believe certain AI infrastructure stocks offer far stronger long-term potential at a much more attractive entry point. If you are looking for an AI stock more promising than SIMO that operates as a critical AI tollbooth and stands as the most important company in the world, check out our report about this must-own AI stock .

news.Content:
We just published the list of 10 Best Memory Stocks to Buy According to Billionaires and Rambus Inc (NASDAQ:RMBS) ranked 8th on the list.

In the first half of the year, memory was the hottest AI trade. Hyperscalers poured billions of dollars into data centers where high-bandwidth memory was one of the tightest bottlenecks in the supply chain. One advantage it has over some of the names on our list is that it gets paid for each chip it ships, so a fall in memory prices hurts it less than it hurts the memory makers. If that holds, the P/E falls to about 14x by 2028. The balance sheet is clean. Rambus holds about $777 million in cash against $20 million in debt, making it essentially debt-free. For a company that benefits from the memory boom with less price risk, I think the multiples look pretty reasonable.

Hedge fund interest grew strongly, with the number holding Rambus climbing from 35 in Q1 to 50 in Q2. The value of their stakes also rose from $461.6 million to $848.0 million.

news.Title: Here’s Why Lumentum (LITE) Was Downgraded
news.Content:
We just published a list of the Analysts Just Sounded the Alarm on These 10 Overhyped Stocks and Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) ranked 9th on this list.

Wall Street had a rough week, and the damage came fast. Thursday's sell-off erased $2.3 trillion in market value, pushed the Nasdaq into a correction and sent the VIX, the market's fear gauge, up 70% to 28, Yahoo Finance reported on November 6. A chip-sector index that plunged 12% on Thursday bounced 4% the next day, and oil fell below $100 a barrel.

Politics added to the swings. The Dow roared back on Wednesday after the midterm results removed election uncertainty, and oil fell on hopes of a deal with Iran, according to Yahoo Finance on November 5, though the rally was already cooling.

Interest rates became the bigger worry. Payrolls rose by 165,000 in October, far above the 65,000 economists expected, while unemployment slipped to 4.1% from 4.2%, Reuters reported on November 6.

Photo by Arturo Añez on Unsplash

Hot Jobs Data Raises the Odds of a Rate Hike

Traders read the numbers as a sign the Federal Reserve is not done tightening. Bets on a rate hike at the next meeting rose to 78% from 70% before the report, and the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.87%. The 30-year yield reached 5.27%.

Chief market economist Peter Cardillo said the labor market is at full employment and that the Fed has no choice but to raise rates in December. Chief investment strategist Susannah Streeter called the report hawkish and said she sees a couple of hikes before late next year, depending on the Iran conflict. Chief economic strategist Brian Jacobsen noted that wages rose 3.1% from a year earlier, yet real wages fell as inflation outpaced them, which he called the affordability crisis in one stat.

What Past Fear Spikes Have Meant for Stocks

Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi pointed to CBOE data showing eight earlier VIX jumps of this size since 1991. The S&P 500 gained an average of 3.0% one month later and 14.7% one year later. Our list of oversold AI stocks where Wall Street analysts are spotting 50%+ upside covers names that have been through a similar reset.

Hiring itself looks steady. Andy Challenger, who tracks corporate job cuts, called the current climate a "low-fire environment," with employers holding on to workers ahead of the holidays, according to Yahoo Finance on November 5.

Not everyone sees a hike as certain. Joe Saluzzi, co-head of equity trading at a New Jersey firm, called the jobs numbers very good but said the recent volatility could lead the Fed to hold off at its next meeting. Readers who follow the market's leaders can see our ranking of the best stocks near all-time highs according to Wall Street .

Story Continues

Lumentum has an average upside potential of 104%, based on analysts' average price target, and had 111 hedge fund holders in Q2 2026.

B. Riley downgraded Lumentum to Neutral from Buy on November 3 and set a $770 price target, down from $1,142, after Marvell's offer for the company. The offer was worth about $1,132 a share to Lumentum holders when announced.

The business behind it keeps growing. CEO Michael Hurlston told investors Lumentum landed its second major win in co-packaged and near-packaged optics, backed by purchase commitments of more than $5 billion. Those are orders customers have committed to before the parts ship, which gives the company a clear view of what it will sell.

Revenue rose 136.5% from a year earlier, led by pump lasers and optical circuit switches. The systems side of the business, which includes the switches, grew much faster than the components side. Hurlston expects about $350 million of added revenue in the fiscal second quarter, with profit margins widening again, and he sees optical switching growing into a multi-billion-dollar annual business. Marvell singled out Lumentum's laser designs and indium phosphide manufacturing as key additions. news.Title: Why Marvell Technology Stock Plunged 28.1% This Week
news.Content:
An agreement to acquire optical components provider Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) in an all-stock transaction valued at $115 billion sent Marvell Technology down 28.1% this week.

Marvell Technology stock changed hands at $141.20 as of the close on Friday, Nov. 6, having dropped 32% from Friday, Oct. 30's close, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence . Over the same period, the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 2.7%, and the Nasdaq-100 was down 4.9%.

Image source: Getty Images.

A $115 billion optical deal sparks heavy dilution concerns

On Monday, Marvell disclosed an agreement to acquire Lumentum at an enterprise value of $115 billion. Under the terms of the all-stock deal, the buyer will issue 4.5 of its own shares for every Lumentum share outstanding. In an all-stock transaction, issuing new shares expands the total share count, diluting existing shareholders by reducing their percentage ownership of future earnings while handing a significant portion of the combined entity to the target owners. Wall Street reacted swiftly: analysts at Bank of America cut their rating to neutral, and TD Cowen downgraded the stock to hold, noting that $1 billion in projected annual cost cuts falls far short of offsetting a roughly 50% increase in share count.

Lumentum manufactures laser components and optical transceivers that convert light signals into electronic data inside high-speed networks. Combining those optical lasers with Marvell's electronic digital signal processors allows the buyer to offer integrated optical interconnect modules for data centers. However, regulators in China and the U.S. must approve the tie-up, a process management expects could stretch into early 2028. Analysts also warned that Lumentum competes with several of Marvell's existing chip customers, creating potential channel conflicts during the multi-year closing window.

Marvell Technology sells wired networking and data infrastructure chips that process and move data within data centers and telecommunications networks to cloud providers and equipment makers. While adding optical laser manufacturing expands the target market for artificial intelligence connectivity, paying a fivefold premium over Lumentum's share price from a year ago strains balance-sheet discipline. Marvell's $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum shifts the investment case from a high-margin data center chip growth story to a complex, dilutive integration bet with years of regulatory uncertainty.

What's next for Marvell Technology

Story Continues

Investors will get their next operational update when Marvell reports fiscal third-quarter results on Dec. 1, 2026. Management narrowed its preliminary quarterly revenue guidance to approximately $3.2 billion, but near-term financial results are taking a back seat to deal execution risks. The stock is down 57.2% (as of the close on Friday, Nov. 6) from its 52-week high of $329.88, reflecting how sharply sentiment turned following the merger news.

Marvell trades at a trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 52.6. Marvell's trailing price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 46.5 sits in the middle of a wide peer group, including Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) at 37.5, Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) at 96, and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) at 9.3, so the multiple on its own does not say whether the stock is cheap; execution on its core data center chip business does.

Is Marvell Technology stock a buy?

By uniting its strengths in electrical and optical interconnect with Lumentum's proficiency in high-performance lasers and optical transceivers, Marvell sees the acquisition as a major step in its drive to become a leader in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.

The prospect of shareholder dilution from the acquisition and the current pushback from communities over the development of AI data centers, however, suggest that investors should be wary of the rosy picture Marvell's management is painting. As a result, investors with Marvell stock on their radars may want to continue watching from the sideline for the time being, waiting for the tech stock to dip further before considering a position.

news.Title: Astera Labs Just Crushed Earnings—So Why Are Analysts Cutting Price Targets?
news.Content: Key Points Interested in Astera Labs, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better. Astera Labs reported Q3 revenue growth of 153.6% to $584.9 million and adjusted EPS of $1.32, both topping analyst estimates on strong Scorpio product demand. Despite the strong results and bullish Q4 guidance, analysts trimmed price targets citing valuation concerns, though most maintained a long-term bullish outlook on the stock. Institutional investors own more than 60% of shares and have consistently accumulated the stock since its IPO, reflecting confidence in Astera Labs' market position. Price action triggered by Astera Labs' (NASDAQ: ALAB) Q3 earnings release isn't all that surprising, given the response to other reports and signals reflected across the tech landscape.hearthear As strong as the Q3 results were, they merely reaffirmed what the market already knows: the AI trade is maturing. → Duolingo's User Growth Is Outpacing Bookings, But Is Its Strategy Paying Off? Doubt and fear that the AI build won't continue, compounded by high valuations, are in play, but an opportunity has emerged. Together, they are pushing stock prices down and creating a deep-value opportunity in the winning stocks. → 3 Dividend ETFs Offer Different Ways to Navigate the Post-Election Sell-Off As the AI trade matures, investors are shifting from broad speculation about AI's potential and its eventual winners, which helped lift much of the technology sector, toward a smaller group of companies delivering tangible results. These companies, like Astera Labs, are securing design wins that can support revenue over multiple years, providing the nuts and bolts to build giant AI computers. The bad news, or rather, the opportunity, is that the good companies are being punished along with the bad, but that will likely change over the coming quarters, driven by performance. → Arista Networks Cashes In on the AI Infrastructure Buildout The technical charts for Astera Labs and Credo Technology Group (NASDAQ: CRDO), another connectivity leader, suggest that both stocks have completed or are nearing the end of an Elliott Wave cycle, presenting two possible scenarios. The first is that the AI boom and bust is over, and ALAB, along with CRDO, are down for the count. The other is that the AI build continues, results align with the growth outlook, and market sentiment recovers. In that scenario, the first Elliott Wave Cycle becomes the first stage in a much larger cycle that can take this market to new highs before the end of next year. Story Continues Astera Labs' Q3 Earnings Show AI Demand Is Still Accelerating Astera Labs Q3 results echo the message in reports from Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), onsemi (NASDAQ: ON), Oracle (NASDAQ: ORCL), and NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ: NXPI), to mention a few. That is, AI demand is strong, broad-based, and accelerating, driven by ramping production of next-gen products. Astera Labs' revenue grew by 153.6% to $584.9 million, exceeding the $550.8 million analyst consensus estimate, driven by strength in the Scorpio line. Scorpio is the newest and now largest product family, smart fabric switches essential to linking massive GPU clusters into an efficient, cohesive operating unit. Astera Labs' margin news was what the market wanted, revealing strong revenue and scale leverage. While gross margin compressed, operating efficiency and spending control shone through, with GAAP operating income rising to $179.1 million from $55.4 million a year earlier and adjusted net income climbing to $243.4 million from $88.2 million. On the bottom line, $1.32 in adjusted earnings per share (EPS) is also up more than 100% and outperformed the analyst consensus by more than 10%, playing into management's decision to issue hot guidance. Guidance is bullish for this market, regardless of the stock price response to the news. Management expects Q4 revenue of $730 million to $750 million and adjusted EPS of $1.62 to $1.66, with the low ends of both ranges exceeding analyst expectations. The outlook may also prove conservative, given the company's competitive advantages, particularly its Scorpio product line. Astera Labs has established an early lead in high-volume PCIe Gen 6 switching, with Scorpio production and a lever for exponential growth: multiple design wins across numerous customers and end markets. It is important that investors understand the difference between design wins and sales. Unlike an immediate sale, a design win can create a multi-year revenue opportunity as customers incorporate Astera Labs' technology into their products and expand production. Some of these programs could generate substantial incremental revenue as they scale. As Astera's largest and fastest-growing line, Scorpio has already topped a $1 billion run-rate and is likely to accelerate in the coming year. Analysts Deflate Outlook, But Maintain Bullish Stance Analysts' responses to the news highlight the near-term valuation headwind and long-term opportunity. While most reduced their price targets, analysts generally maintained a bullish long-term outlook, citing valuation concerns and broader market conditions as reasons to limit near-term expectations. The average analyst price target currently implies around 68% upside and is up approximately 77% over the past year. Institutional activity also reflects a bullish posture. The group owns more than 60% of the shares and has bought on balance every quarter since the IPO through early Q4 2026. The risk is that they shed shares and add momentum to the downturn; the company's strong market position, profitability, and history of institutional accumulation could help limit that risk. Profitability is a primary factor in the ongoing market-wide shift; companies that aren't profitable and lack revenue will likely be left behind in the subsequent recovery, while stocks like ALAB are positioned to lead. news.Title: These 4 Stocks Are Tied to the Smartphone in Your Pocket
news.Content:
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM), Corning (NYSE:GLW), and Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) each collect a share of the money spent on smartphones. Apple sells the phone. Qualcomm supplies chips and patent licenses, Corning makes the glass over the screen, and Arm's chip designs turn up in almost all smartphones.

But their latest quarterly reports all vary meaningfully. Apple's iPhone revenue climbed 17% year over year in the September quarter, while Qualcomm's handset chip revenue dropped 26%. And Corning and Arm both said a softer smartphone market hurt their results.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

All four also pointed to the same pressure: memory chips have become much pricier. But I think it matters really differently for each stock.

Image source: Getty Images.

1. Apple's iPhone is still growing

Apple makes much more money from the phone than the other three do. iPhone sales were around $254 billion for fiscal 2026, which ended Sept. 26. That was 53% of Apple's revenue and 21% more than a year earlier.

But growth is slowing. iPhone revenue climbed 17% year over year to $57.6 billion in the fiscal fourth quarter, after gaining around 22% in fiscal Q3. And excluding the benefit of tariff refunds, Apple's gross margin dipped about one point from the June quarter. Management sees it coming in between 45% and 46% in the holiday quarter, mainly because of memory costs.

At roughly $347 as of this writing, Apple trades at about 36 times its expected fiscal 2027 earnings . Investors are paying a premium as its margins fall.

2. Qualcomm's handset slide is getting steeper

Qualcomm's phone business is going the other way. Its handset chip revenue dropped 26% year over year to around $5.1 billion in its fiscal fourth quarter, which ended Sept. 27. It had risen 3% in fiscal Q1, then dropped 13% in Q2 and 20% in Q3. For the full fiscal year, Qualcomm blamed lower shipments to some major phone makers, which cut their build plans as memory got scarcer and pricier.

And Qualcomm expects Apple to rely mostly on its own modems from now on, a change it warns will significantly hit its chip sales.

Of course, Qualcomm still collects from the phone through its patents. It renewed its long-term license with Apple, and licensing kept 70% of its revenue as pre-tax profit in the quarter, versus 24% for the chip business. Meanwhile, auto chip revenue surged 89% to nearly $2 billion.

Story Continues

At roughly $150, Qualcomm trades at about 15 times the earnings it's expected to report in fiscal 2027. I'd say the price already assumes the handset business keeps shrinking.

3. Corning: the glass is the smaller business

Corning's links with Apple stretch back almost 20 years.

"By the end of 2026, all the cover glass for iPhone, including iPhone Duo, and Apple Watch, sold worldwide will be produced at our Harrodsburg, Kentucky facility," chief financial officer Ed Schlesinger said on Corning's Oct. 27 earnings call.

Phone glass, though, is in Corning's glass innovations segment, which also sells glass for TVs and laptops. Segment sales slipped 3% in the third quarter, to about $1.5 billion, and segment net income slid 10%.

Optical communications, meanwhile, grew sales 44% to around $2.4 billion, and Corning's sales linked to generative AI more than doubled. With shares near $104, Corning trades at about 23 times next year's expected earnings, a price I think largely depends on fiber.

4. A royalty on nearly every phone

About 43% of Arm's royalties in the fiscal year ended March 31 came from the main smartphone processors.

In the September quarter, royalty revenue dropped to $670 million, down from $715 million three months earlier, and grew just 8% year over year. Arm said memory prices hit the smartphone market, partly offsetting a doubling in data center royalties.

Around $166 as of this writing, Arm stock trades at about 55 times expected earnings for fiscal 2028, which for Arm ends in March 2028. Investors are probably paying that premium for the data center, where Arm expects Arm-based chips to make up more than 60% of the server market at the largest cloud providers by the end of 2026.

The one I'd own for the phone

Ultimately, of the four, only Apple reported growing phone sales last quarter.

Sure, about 36 times expected earnings isn't cheap, and memory costs might pressure Apple's margins for a while. But Apple sets the device's price, and it raised iPhone prices in September. Qualcomm is much cheaper, but its handset revenue is still falling.

For the phone itself, I'd consider buying Apple.

news.Title: 華邦電董座談新唐：產能包袱將降；AI轉型漸收效
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-07 17:01:48 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電(2344)今(7)日舉辦零碳家庭日，董事長焦佑鈞(附圖)針對旗下新唐(4919)近期接班分工的調整做出說明，將新唐董事長、執行長職務分開，由集團過去十年刻意培養的吳孟奇擔任執行長，係負責日本公司的調整、重整，以及推動未來發展；而過去兩年新唐轉向AI的研發布局，則預期可望在明(2027)年、2028年陸續看到成果。

焦佑鈞指出，新唐目前仍處虧損，主要係負擔來自日本新唐與Tower的合資工廠，相關安排涉及49%持股及須負責的產能。疫情期間市場缺產能，問題並不明顯，但疫情後產能過剩，便造成較大的財務負擔。目前已與Tower談妥，自2027年4月1日起解除相關合作，屆時產能包袱可望獲得解決，他認為，新唐營運狀況將隨之好轉。

除了處理既有負擔，新唐也持續調整成長方向。焦佑鈞回顧，2019年評估日本業務時，原先看重的是進入日本及汽車電子市場的機會，但近年汽車市場並未特別成長，成長動能主要來自AI領域。因此，過去兩年在原董事長帶領下，新唐全力將研發資源轉往AI相關領域，目前已打下一些基礎，隨著開發進度推進，2027~2028年將陸續看到成果。

至於原新唐董事長退休後的安排，焦佑鈞表示，正值記憶體景氣熱絡、華邦電大量投資之際，集團希望將其記憶體經驗帶回華邦電，因此安排擔任高級顧問，待其2027年1月自新唐退休後，再評估如何進一步協助記憶體業務。他也以「賠錢很煩，賺錢很累」形容經營挑戰並指出，景氣好時同業都在搶人才、設備及推進技術，企業仍須持續投入，不能因當期獲利良好就放慢腳步。

news.Title: 華邦電2026零碳家庭日登場，董座：今年業績非常好、獎金非常多
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】記憶體大廠華邦電(2344)今（7）日於雲林劍湖山世界主題樂園舉辦「2026零碳家庭日」，以「綠遊劍湖山」為主題，邀請北中南各地員工及眷屬齊聚同歡。這是華邦電連續第五年推動零碳家庭日，今年參與員工與家屬超過五千人，也致贈每位在職員工一只大同電鍋。董事長焦佑鈞在致詞時也揭露，今年公司業績非常好，獎金也非常多。為落實低碳活動理念，華邦電今日家庭日，安排專車接送各地員工及眷屬，透過集中運輸降低交通碳排放，並以自購碳權抵銷活動全程的碳足跡，實踐零碳家庭日的核心精神。此外，今年特別致贈每位在職員工大同電鍋乙只，將企業關懷延伸至員工家庭，持續營造兼顧員工福祉與永續價值的友善職場環境。

華邦電持續深化綠色製造與資源循環，2026年旗下生產製造廠全數通過UL 2799廢棄物零填埋（Zero Waste to Landfill）最高鉑金級認證，並榮獲環境部「淨水永續 水處理卓越獎」，展現華邦在廢棄物管理、智慧低碳管理及水資源循環等面向的實踐成果。透過系統化管理與技術創新，持續提升資源使用效率，包括將製程廢硫酸再生回用於廠內系統，落實循環經濟；同時，中科廠結合物聯網（IoT）與人工智慧（AI）技術優化廢水處理流程，使氟廢水處理系統每年減少4.5%的化學藥劑使用量，並透過製程優化增加每年355噸濃磷酸回收量，有效落實源頭減量，減輕環境負荷，展現智慧製造與環境永續的整合效益。

此次零碳家庭日不僅凝聚員工與家屬的情感，也展現華邦電將永續理念融入企業文化與日常生活的具體實踐。秉持「以綠色半導體技術豐富人類生活的隱形冠軍」之企業願景，華邦將持續推動智慧製造與資源循環，落實低碳營運，穩步邁向淨零目標。

news.Title: 華邦電焦佑鈞坦言『賠錢很煩，賺錢很累』，員工今年大概可領30個月
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】記憶體產業大多頭，本土記憶體大廠華邦電(2344)董座焦佑鈞坦言『賠錢很煩，賺錢很累』。至於今年華邦電員工可以領入多少總薪資金，他提到，估算是30個月。焦佑鈞指出，賠錢很煩，需要把企業轉虧為盈，但賺錢的時候也很累。他細說，大家都賺錢，大家都向前衝、創造技術，同時為了有更多產出，大家都在找人、搶設備，但也不能說，自己今年賺錢很舒服，就不繼續向前走，反而別人賺錢就讓他向錢衝，因為這樣會讓自己過三年就垮了，所以賺錢也是很累。

華邦電今年獲利會非常好，外界也在社群平台流傳員工今年平均可領約30個月獎金，焦佑鈞透露，有估算的確是30個月。但他也補充，分紅分潤屬於公司制度，這種事情員工是不應該說出來的，也因為這件事情造成記憶體同業的困擾，自己心裡也不安。

他提到也有可能是員工的家屬知道後太過興奮就在社群媒體分享，消息也就傳開了，但公司過去對於相關的薪籌制度是有規定的，員工都清楚這件事，會在今天的家庭日，提醒員工和他們的家人要留意，不要因為一時興奮而造成影響，員工會受罰的。

至於華邦電今年獲利良好，明年又是公司成立40周年，會不會進行結構性調薪，或以其他方式獎勵員工？焦佑鈞表示，公司股利與員工獎金都有制度規範，依章程規定，股利分配至少要達一定比例，且大部分會以現金發放。

華邦電下個月會配發每股2元，這是依照章程，根據上半年獲利進行分配。而員工獎金也有明確制度，會依營業利益的一定比例提撥。每季財報公布後，同仁就能依照公司規定推估獎金總額；實際分配時，還會納入個人考核因素。

news.Title: 記憶體漲價有極限！華邦電董座示警AI獨旺、百業蕭條，恐壓抑消費買氣
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】近期針對記憶體售價太高，影響包括手機、筆電等終端市場消費性買氣，華邦電(2344)董事長焦佑鈞坦言，自己也認為，現在的景氣有點像「百業蕭條，只有AI一枝獨秀」，記憶體持續漲價會增加一般消費者的負擔，因此價格上漲有其極限。焦佑鈞形容，現在的景氣有點像「百業蕭條，只有AI一枝獨秀」。他補充，手機、PC和許多電子產品的銷售都不如以往，但AI需求對漲價的承受度較高，不過一般消費者，會因為手機或PC價格太高，延後換機。

因此，他認為記憶體的售價持續上漲，會增加一般消費者的負擔，因此價格上漲有其極限。焦佑鈞也補充，自己常說，不能讓AI把所有資源都用掉，其他產業和消費者也需要正常生活。

而就記憶體價格是否已經到頂，焦佑鈞表示，自己希望是！因為再漲下去，對一般消費者會造成更大的傷害。此外，現下記憶體廠毛利率已站上七成，部分甚至達到八成，對此，他提到，自己不認為毛利率可以無止境地上升，因為任何事情都有極限，目前市場看到的限制之一，就是資金。

焦佑鈞也提到，2029年可能是下一個景氣下行週期的時間點，然華邦電董事會近日通過731.63億元資本支出投入高雄廠Module B2的建置，焦佑鈞補充，這個投資是為了再一波景氣上揚趨勢，2030年～2031年多頭所準備的產能。

news.Title: 華邦電董座看明後年AI需求穩；盼記憶體止漲
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-07 16:49:05 周佩宇 發佈

華邦電(2344)今(7)日舉辦零碳家庭日，針對AI發展展望，董事長焦佑鈞(附圖)在媒體餐敘時做出說明，依客戶回饋，明(2027)、2028年資料中心(DC)裝機量已有先前投資支撐，相關DRAM需求明確，而供給則取決於供應鏈增產速度，不過AI以外的消費性電子需求已受高價影響，從社會責任角度來看，記憶體漲價差不多到極限了。

焦佑鈞指出，目前AI需求一枝獨秀，對價格上漲仍能接受，但手機、PC等消費性電子產品不同，當終端價格變貴，消費者就會考慮將手機、電腦多用一年，延後換機，持續漲價反而衝擊需求，相對整個供應鏈仍須兼顧不同應用的承受能力。

至於近期美國期中選舉影響市場對AI發展的信心，他指出，就資料中心需求，2027、2028年的裝機量已有先前投資支撐，相關DRAM需求明確，而供給則取決於供應鏈增產速度。他說明，資料中心須提前取得土地開發許可、完成廠房等基礎建設，同時目前2027年的裝機前準備已完成，2028年預期也不會受到太大影響。

不過資金限制將恐為2029年下一波下行循環的重要原因，且屆時是否仍有足夠的廠房、電力、土地支持大量投資，仍須持續向客戶確認。他也回顧，原先曾以兩年估算本波上升循環，自2025年7月起算約至2027年6月；如今景氣延續至2028、2029年，業者可能不斷上修擴產計畫，反而累積過多供給，使後續修正更急、調整期更長，因此上升循環拖得越久，未必全是好事。

華邦電供給方面，自2025年下半年啟動的擴產目前正陸續裝機，2027年將有較多產出供應市場，2028年仍會增加，但因潔淨室空間已滿，增幅將較2027年縮小。

至於收購英飛凌記憶體業務，焦佑鈞說明，標的無自有晶圓廠，品牌與人員將保留，供貨來自原有晶圓代工產能，華邦電不須承接工廠管理，也沒有另赴德州建廠的規劃，後續其產品擴上，充仍須搭配自身擴產。

最後在獲利回饋方面，焦佑鈞表示，依目前獲利與既有制度估算，2026年員工平均可望有約30個月獎金，個人分配上仍須納入考核；公司也預計12月發放上半年度每股2元現金股利。他形容，「賠錢很煩，但賺錢很累」，因為同業都在找人才、搶設備及推進技術，即使當期獲利良好，仍須持續投入，才能維持未來競爭力。

news.Title: 景氣太好反而危險！焦佑鈞憂2029年恐迎下行週期，慎防產能過剩
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】關於這波大環境或是記憶體多頭可以走多久，華邦電(2344)董事長焦佑鈞估計，景氣的下行週期可能發生在2029年，而自己比較擔心的是，不景氣來得太晚，因為景氣好得太久，業者可能不知道什麼時候該停下來，而持續擴建，最後就可能形成過剩產能。他提到，兩年前自己曾預估這一波景氣上行約兩年，從2025年7月開始計算，兩年大約到2027年6月，當時很多人談超級循環，認為景氣會持續很久；但現在連正常週期都還沒走完，市場已經開始擔心後續走勢。

他坦言，如果景氣上行真的只有兩年，那壞消息就是兩年後可能進入下行週期；好消息則是下行兩年後可能再度復甦。現在讓市場感到不安的是，景氣可能延續到2028年或2029年，但也可能更早反轉，時間點仍不明朗。

就近期股價震盪非常劇烈，修正的原因，究竟是反映的是基本面，還是市場對未來的預期，焦佑鈞表示，自己不方便評論資本市場，因為市場考量的因素很多，現階段該做的就是把自己的工作做好，而最近幾天的波動，可能也和美國期中選舉有關；至於美國選後的政策與後續動向，華邦電和自己都會持續密切關注。

news.Title: AI資料中心錢已到位！華邦電董座稱2027、2028年無虞，2029年才是關鍵
news.Content:
【財訊快報／記者李純君報導】全球股市劇烈修正、費半與台股大暴跌，除美國選舉有關外，市場擔心是否與CSP業者在AI資料中心投資過於龐大、資金無法回收、自由現金受限有關，對此，華邦電(2344)董事長焦佑鈞表示，2027年和2028年所需要建置AI資料中心的資金都已經規劃或是籌措好了，這兩年是設備安裝期，要擔心的反而是2029年。焦佑鈞說，AI資料中心建置需要很多錢，能否回收，以及相關業者是否已經遭遇自由現金流受限等議題，其實已經討論半年到一年，不是現在才存在或是現在才討論的問題。

他直言，自己和華邦電都一直把資金來源視為觀察資料中心投資循環的重要指標，而整體經濟最終還是要看有多少資金可以投入；如果資金不足，投資一定會放慢。因此，自己原本就認為，到了2029年，資金限制可能成為下一波景氣下行的原因。

他透露，從客戶端了解的狀況，這一波相關資金可能已經支出，或已從資本市場取得，因此2027、2028年的建置有既定基礎；2029年則是另一個需要持續評估的問題。換言之，這一波要建AI資料中心的錢都已經準備好或是規劃好了，甚至已經支付，後續只是機器設備在2027、2028年移入，因此自由現金流的壓力已反映在先前的資金安排中。

他提到，資料中心建置需要經過土地開發許可、電力與廠房等程序。以2027年來看，相關土地許可已取得，電力與廠房也已到位，接下來主要是安裝伺服器。因此，2027年的建置目前看來不太會受到資金或開發許可影響，2028年預期也不會有太大影響。焦佑鈞補充，這些資訊是華邦電根據過去一年向客戶詢問所得的訊息統整。

焦佑鈞也直言，2027年、2028年主要是既有基礎建設完成後的設備安裝期，至於2029年是否還有足夠的廠房、電力與土地，讓CSP維持目前的投資規模，還需要持續了解，以及2029年CSP業者是否有錢再繼續進行下一波的，目前客戶尚未提供2029年的明確規劃，可能要等明年拜訪時再進一步確認。

news.Title: 華邦電今年業績佳　員工獎金平均30個月
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中雲林2026年11月7日電）記憶體廠華邦電 (2344) 今天在劍湖山世界舉辦家庭日活動，董事長焦佑鈞表示，今年業績非常好，員工獎金非常多，估計平均獎金約30個月。

華邦電今天的家庭日活動約有2600名員工參與，若加計眷屬有超過5000人。焦佑鈞說，參加的人數再創新高。感謝所有眷屬對於員工的支持，讓他們能夠安心在公司工作，戰戰兢兢努力為公司創造良好的成績。

隨著期中選舉結束，市場憂心美國人工智慧（AI）政策可能出現變化，焦佑鈞表示，一定會對資料中心建置造成影響，只是影響程度仍待進一步觀察。

他指出，資料中心建置需要做很多事，包含取得土地開發許可，以及建置基礎設施等，已完成營建的資料中心將陸續安裝伺服器，預期2027年和2028年資料中心市場應不受期中選舉結果影響。

焦佑鈞說，雲端服務供應商（CSP）自由現金流轉負的情況已經發生，華邦電將資金來源視為研判景氣循環的觀察指標，因為如果沒有錢，所有的投資一定會減緩，初步估計2029年資金限制將是景氣反轉的原因。

針對華邦電董事會核准新台幣731.63億元資本支出，用以擴建高雄廠模組B建廠及生產設備投資，焦佑鈞表示，這並不是為了這波景氣，而是為了2031年及2032年下一波景氣攀升預作準備。

對於記憶體廠毛利率表現，焦佑鈞說，任何事情都有其極限，漲價也是一樣，現在是百業蕭條一枝獨秀，唯有AI好，手機、個人電腦等電子產品銷售都比以前不好，繼續漲價，一般的消費者會受到傷害，希望記憶體價格已經到頂。

焦佑鈞表示，賠錢很煩，因為要想辦法能夠賺錢，賺錢很累，因為要找人、創新技術。華邦電決定斥資11.2億美元現金，約新台幣353.92億元，取得英飛凌NOR Flash與F-RAM事業100%股權，就是基於人才考量。
